title.zh: 卷84 列傳第49 北狄
title.raw: 卷84 列傳第49 北狄 Volume 84 Biographies 49: The Beidi

sentences.zh: 突厥之先，平涼雜胡也，姓阿史那氏。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Turks were mixed Hu people from Pingliang, surnamed Ashina.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks traced their origins to the mixed Hu peoples of Pingliang and bore the surname Ashina.

sentences.zh: 後魏太武滅沮渠氏，阿史那以五百家奔茹茹，世居金山，工於鐵作。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Later Wei destroyed the Juqu clan, the Ashina, five hundred households, fled to the Rouran and dwelt for generations on Jinshan, skilled in ironworking.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei destroyed the Juqu clan, five hundred Ashina households fled to the Rouran and settled for generations on Mount Jin, where they became expert smiths.

sentences.zh: 金山狀如兜鍪，俗呼兜鍪爲「突厥」，因以爲號。

translations.literal: Jinshan was shaped like a helmet; the common people called a helmet "Tujue," and on this basis they took it as their name.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jin resembled a helmet, and since helmets were commonly called "Tujue" in their tongue, they adopted that as their name.

sentences.zh: 或云，其先國於西海之上，爲鄰國所滅，男女無少長盡殺之。

translations.literal: Some say their ancestral state lay west of the sea and was destroyed by a neighboring kingdom, which slaughtered every man and woman, young and old, without exception.
translations.idiomatic: According to tradition, their forebears once had a state west of the sea until a neighboring power annihilated it, killing men and women of all ages without mercy.

sentences.zh: 至一兒，不忍殺，刖足斷臂，棄於大澤中。

translations.literal: When it came to one boy, they could not bear to kill him; they cut off his feet and severed his arms and cast him into a great marsh.
translations.idiomatic: One infant boy they spared from death—but only after mutilating his feet and cutting off his arms before abandoning him in a vast swamp.

sentences.zh: 有一牝狼，每銜肉至其所，此兒因食之，得以不死。

translations.literal: A she-wolf brought meat to him every day; the boy ate it and so did not die.
translations.idiomatic: A she-wolf regularly brought him meat, and by eating what she brought, the boy survived.

sentences.zh: 其後遂與狼交，狼有孕焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter he mated with the wolf, and the wolf became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: In time he coupled with the wolf, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 彼鄰國者，復令人殺此兒，而狼在其側。

translations.literal: That neighboring kingdom again sent men to kill this boy, while the wolf was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring kingdom sent men once more to kill the boy, but the wolf remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 使者將殺之，其狼若爲神所憑，欻然至於海東，止於山上。

translations.literal: As the emissaries were about to kill him, the wolf, as though possessed by a spirit, suddenly came to the eastern sea and stopped on a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the envoys were about to strike, the wolf—seeming possessed by a spirit—swept eastward across the sea and halted on a mountain.

sentences.zh: 其山在高昌西北，下有洞穴，狼入其中，遇得平壤茂草，地方二百餘里。

translations.literal: The mountain lay northwest of Gaochang; below it was a cave into which the wolf entered and found level ground with luxuriant grass covering more than two hundred li square.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain stood northwest of Gaochang. A cave at its base led to a broad plain of lush grassland stretching more than two hundred li in every direction.

sentences.zh: 其後狼生十男，其一姓阿史那氏，最賢，遂爲君長，故牙門建狼頭纛，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Thereafter the wolf bore ten sons; one surnamed Ashina was the most worthy and became chieftain. Hence at the gate of the headquarters they raised a wolf-head banner, showing that they did not forget their origin.
translations.idiomatic: The wolf later gave birth to ten sons. The one surnamed Ashina was the most capable and became their chieftain. For this reason a wolf-head banner was erected at the headquarters gate, a reminder never to forget their origins.

sentences.zh: 有阿賢設者，率部落出於穴中，世臣茹茹。

translations.literal: There was one named Axienshe who led the tribe out of the cave and for generations served the Rouran as vassals.
translations.idiomatic: A chieftain named Axienshe led the tribe out of the cave, and for generations they served the Rouran as subjects.

sentences.zh: 至大葉護，種類漸強。

translations.literal: By the time of Dayehu, the clan gradually grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dayehu, the tribe gradually grew in strength.

sentences.zh: 當後魏之末，有伊利可汗，以兵擊鐵勒，大敗之，降五萬餘家，遂求婚於茹茹。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Wei there was Illi Qaghan, who attacked the Tiele with troops, routed them utterly, and received the submission of more than fifty thousand households; he then sought a marriage alliance with the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Northern Wei, Illi Qaghan attacked the Tiele and crushed them, bringing more than fifty thousand households to submission. He then sought a marriage alliance with the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 茹茹主阿那瑰大怒，遣使罵之。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui was greatly angered and sent an envoy to revile him.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran ruler Anagui was furious and sent an envoy to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 伊利斬其使，率衆襲茹茹，破之。

translations.literal: Illi beheaded the envoy and led his forces in a surprise attack on the Rouran, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Illi executed the envoy and led his warriors in a raid against the Rouran, breaking their forces.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟逸可汗立，又破茹茹。

translations.literal: When he died, his younger brother Yi Qaghan succeeded and again defeated the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death, his younger brother Yi Qaghan took the throne and once again routed the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 病且卒，舍其子攝圖，立其弟俟鬥，稱爲木杆可汗。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and was near death, he set aside his son Shetu and installed his younger brother Sidou, who was styled Mughan Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: As illness brought him to death's door, he passed over his son Shetu and installed his younger brother Sidou as Mughan Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 木杆勇而多智，遂擊茹茹，滅之，西破挹怛，東走契丹，北方戎狄悉歸之，抗衡中夏。

translations.literal: Mughan was brave and resourceful; he attacked the Rouran and destroyed them, defeated the Yeda in the west, drove the Khitan eastward, and all the northern barbarians submitted to him, enabling him to contend with the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Mughan was bold and shrewd. He destroyed the Rouran, crushed the Yeda in the west, and drove the Khitan eastward until every northern tribe submitted to him, giving the Turks the power to stand as equals against the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 後與西魏師入侵東魏，至於太原。

translations.literal: Later he joined Western Wei forces in invading Eastern Wei and reached as far as Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later allied with Western Wei armies in an invasion of Eastern Wei that pushed as far as Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其俗畜牧爲事，隨逐水草，不恆厥處。

translations.literal: Their custom was to make animal husbandry their occupation, following water and pasture, without a fixed dwelling place.
translations.idiomatic: They lived by herding livestock, moving with the seasons from pasture to pasture without a permanent home.

sentences.zh: 穹廬氈帳，被髮左衽，食肉飲酪，身衣裘褐，賤老貴壯。

translations.literal: They lived in domed felt tents, wore their hair loose with the left lapel folded over, ate meat and drank fermented milk, clothed themselves in furs and coarse wool, and valued the young while despising the old.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelt in domed felt tents, wore their hair loose with garments folded left over right, subsisted on meat and fermented milk, dressed in furs and coarse wool, and held the young in esteem while looking down on the aged.

sentences.zh: 官有葉護，次設特勤，次俟利發，次吐屯發，下至小官，凡二十八等，皆世爲之。

translations.literal: In office there was the Yehu, next the Sheteqin, next the Yilibo, next the Tutunbo, down to minor officials—twenty-eight grades in all, all hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Their offices included the Yehu, followed by the Sheteqin, the Yilibo, and the Tutunbo, down through twenty-eight ranks of lesser officials—all positions passed down through families.

sentences.zh: 有角弓、鳴鏑、甲、矟、刀、劍。

translations.literal: They had composite bows, whistling arrows, armor, lances, knives, and swords.
translations.idiomatic: Their armaments included composite bows, whistling arrows, armor, lances, knives, and swords.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，性殘忍。

translations.literal: They were skilled at mounted archery and by nature cruel.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at mounted archery and were by nature ruthless.

sentences.zh: 無文字，刻木爲契。

translations.literal: They had no writing and carved wood to make contracts.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written language and recorded agreements by carving marks into wood.

sentences.zh: 候月將滿，輒爲寇抄。

translations.literal: When they awaited the moon nearing fullness, they would invariably raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They typically launched their raids when the moon was nearly full.

sentences.zh: 謀反叛殺人者皆死，淫者割勢而腰斬之。

translations.literal: Those who plotted rebellion or committed murder were all put to death; adulterers had their genitals cut off and were then cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Conspiracy, rebellion, and murder were capital offenses. Adulterers were castrated and then cut in half at the waist.

sentences.zh: 鬥傷人目者償之以女，無女則輸婦財，折支體以輸馬，盜者則償贓十倍。

translations.literal: One who in a fight injured another's eye compensated with a daughter; if he had no daughter, he paid bridal wealth. For broken limbs one paid horses. Thieves compensated tenfold the value of the stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: Injuring someone's eye in a brawl required compensation with a daughter—or bridal wealth if one had no daughter. Broken limbs were compensated with horses. Thieves paid ten times the value of what they stole.

sentences.zh: 有死者，停屍帳中，家人親屬多殺牛馬而祭之，繞帳號呼，以刀劃面，血淚交下，七度而止。

translations.literal: When someone died, the corpse was kept in the tent; family and kin slaughtered many cattle and horses as offerings, circled the tent wailing, cut their faces with knives until blood and tears mingled, stopping after seven rounds.
translations.idiomatic: When a person died, the body was laid out in the tent while family and kin slaughtered cattle and horses as offerings, circled the tent wailing, and cut their faces with knives until blood and tears ran together—repeating this seven times.

sentences.zh: 於是擇日置屍馬上而焚之，取灰而葬。

translations.literal: Then on a chosen day the corpse was placed on a horse and burned; the ashes were taken and buried.
translations.idiomatic: On an auspicious day the body was placed on a horse and cremated, and the ashes were buried.

sentences.zh: 表木爲塋，立屋其中，圖畫死者形儀及其生時所經戰陣之狀。

translations.literal: They marked the tomb with wooden posts and erected a house within, painting the likeness of the deceased and scenes of the battles he had fought in life.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden markers ringed the burial site, and within a house was built bearing painted portraits of the deceased and scenes from the battles he had fought in life.

sentences.zh: 嘗殺一人，則立一石，有至千百者。

translations.literal: For each person one had killed, one erected a stone; some had as many as hundreds or thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Each enemy slain was commemorated with a standing stone; some warriors accumulated hundreds or even thousands.

sentences.zh: 父兄死，子弟妻其群母及嫂。

translations.literal: When a father or elder brother died, the younger men took as wives his stepmothers and sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Upon a father's or elder brother's death, younger men married their stepmothers and sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 五月中，多殺羊馬以祭天，男子好樗蒲，女子踏鞠，飲馬酪取醉，歌呼相對。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they slaughtered many sheep and horses to sacrifice to Heaven. Men enjoyed playing chupu; women played cuju. They drank fermented mare's milk until drunk and sang and shouted to one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they slaughtered sheep and horses as offerings to Heaven. Men gambled at chupu, women played cuju, and all drank fermented mare's milk until drunk, singing and shouting across the camp.

sentences.zh: 敬鬼神，信巫覡，重兵死而恥病終，大抵與匈奴同俗。

translations.literal: They revered ghosts and spirits, trusted shamans, honored death in battle and were ashamed to die of illness; in general their customs were the same as those of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They venerated spirits, trusted shamans, glorified death in battle and scorned dying of illness—in most respects their customs mirrored those of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 木杆在位二十年，卒，復舍其子大邏便而立其弟，是爲佗缽可汗。

translations.literal: Mughan reigned twenty years and died; again setting aside his son Daluobian, he installed his younger brother, who became Töpöl Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Mughan reigned twenty years. Upon his death, his son Daluobian was passed over in favor of his younger brother, who became Töpöl Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 佗缽以攝圖爲爾伏可汗，統其東面，又以其弟褥但可汗子爲步離可汗，居西方。

translations.literal: Töpöl made Shetu Erfu Qaghan, commanding the eastern region; he also made the son of his younger brother Rutan Qaghan Buli Qaghan, who dwelt in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Töpöl appointed Shetu as Erfu Qaghan to govern the east, and made the son of his brother Rutan Qaghan the Buli Qaghan, who held the western territories.

sentences.zh: 時佗缽控弦數十萬，中國憚之，周、齊爭結姻好，傾府藏以事之。

translations.literal: At that time Töpöl commanded several hundred thousand bowmen; the Central States feared him, and Zhou and Qi competed to forge marriage alliances, emptying their treasuries to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Töpöl commanded several hundred thousand warriors, and the Central States trembled before him. Northern Zhou and Northern Qi vied to win his favor through marriage alliances, draining their treasuries to appease him.

sentences.zh: 佗缽益驕，每謂其下曰：「我在南兩兒常孝順，何患貧也！」

translations.literal: Töpöl grew ever prouder and often said to his subordinates: "I have two dutiful sons in the south—why should I worry about poverty!
translations.idiomatic: Töpöl grew increasingly arrogant and often told his followers: "I have two dutiful sons in the south—why should I ever want for anything?"

sentences.zh: 齊有沙門惠琳，被掠入突厥，因謂佗缽曰：「齊國富強者，爲有佛法耳。」

translations.literal: There was a Qi monk named Huilin who was captured and taken among the Turks; he therefore said to Töpöl: "The reason Qi is rich and strong is that it has the Buddhist Dharma."
translations.idiomatic: A Qi monk named Huilin, captured and taken to live among the Turks, told Töpöl: "Qi owes its wealth and power to the Buddhist Dharma."

sentences.zh: 遂說以因緣果報之事。

translations.literal: He then expounded the doctrine of karmic cause and effect.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to teach the doctrine of karmic cause and effect.

sentences.zh: 佗缽聞而信之，建一伽藍，遣使聘于齊氏，求《淨名》、《涅槃》、《華嚴》等經，並《十誦律》。

translations.literal: Töpöl heard and believed; he built a monastery and sent envoys to Qi seeking the Vimalakirti, Nirvana, and Avatamsaka sutras, as well as the Ten Recitations Vinaya.
translations.idiomatic: Töpöl was convinced and built a monastery. He sent envoys to Qi requesting the Vimalakirti, Nirvana, and Avatamsaka sutras, along with the Ten Recitations Vinaya.

sentences.zh: 佗缽亦躬自齋戒，繞塔行道，恨不生內地。

translations.literal: Töpöl also personally observed fasting and precepts, circumambulated pagodas in walking meditation, and regretted that he had not been born in the inner lands.
translations.idiomatic: Töpöl himself observed fasting and precepts, circumambulated pagodas in devout procession, and lamented that he had not been born in the civilized heartland.

sentences.zh: 在位十年，病且卒，謂其子菴羅曰：「吾聞親莫過於父子。

translations.literal: Having reigned ten years, when he fell ill and was near death, he said to his son Anluo: "I have heard that no bond is closer than that between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years on the throne, as illness brought him near death, he told his son Anluo: "I have always heard that no bond runs deeper than that between father and son.

sentences.zh: 吾兄不親其子，委地於我。

translations.literal: My elder brother did not favor his own son but entrusted the land to me.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother passed over his own son and entrusted the realm to me instead.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝當避大邏便也。」

translations.literal: When I die, you must keep clear of Daluobian.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you must stay clear of Daluobian."

sentences.zh: 及佗鉢卒，國中將立大邏便，以其母賤，眾不服。

translations.literal: When Töpöl died, the realm was about to install Daluobian, but because his mother was of low status the people would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: After Töpöl's death, the realm prepared to install Daluobian, but the people refused to accept him because his mother was of low birth.

sentences.zh: 菴羅母貴，突厥素重之。

translations.literal: Anluo's mother was of noble rank, and the Turks had always held her in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo's mother was of noble lineage, and the Turks had long held her in high regard.

sentences.zh: 攝圖最後至，謂國中曰：「若立菴羅者，我當率兄弟以事之；

translations.literal: Shetu arrived last and said to the realm: "If Anluo is installed, I shall lead my brothers in serving him;
translations.idiomatic: Shetu arrived last and addressed the assembly: "If Anluo is chosen, I and my brothers will serve him faithfully;

sentences.zh: 如立大邏便，我必守境，利刃長矛以相待矣。」

translations.literal: but if Daluobian is installed, I shall certainly hold the borderlands and meet you with sharp blades and long spears.
translations.idiomatic: but if Daluobian is chosen, I will hold my territory and greet you with drawn blades and leveled spears."

sentences.zh: 攝圖長而且雄，國人皆憚，莫敢拒者，竟以菴羅爲嗣。

translations.literal: Shetu was tall and imposing; all in the realm feared him and none dared refuse. In the end Anluo was made successor.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu was tall and formidable, and everyone feared him. None dared oppose him, and Anluo was ultimately installed as successor.

sentences.zh: 大邏便不得立，心不服菴羅，每遣人罵辱之。

translations.literal: Daluobian was not installed; in his heart he would not submit to Anluo and repeatedly sent men to revile and humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the throne, Daluobian refused to accept Anluo's authority and repeatedly sent men to revile and humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 菴羅不能制，因以國讓攝圖。

translations.literal: Anluo could not control the situation and therefore ceded the realm to Shetu.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to contain the situation, Anluo yielded the realm to Shetu.

sentences.zh: 國中相與議曰：「四可汗之子，攝圖最賢。」

translations.literal: The realm deliberated together, saying: "Among the four qaghans' sons, Shetu is the most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly deliberated: "Among the four qaghans' sons, Shetu is the most capable."

sentences.zh: 因迎立之，號伊利俱盧設莫何始波羅可汗，一號沙缽略。

translations.literal: They therefore welcomed and installed him, styling him Illi Gul Shemohe Shiboluo Qaghan, also known as Ishbara.
translations.idiomatic: They welcomed and installed him, giving him the title Illi Gul Shemohe Shiboluo Qaghan, also known as Ishbara.

sentences.zh: 治都斤山。

translations.literal: He ruled from Mount Dujin.
translations.idiomatic: He established his court at Mount Dujin.

sentences.zh: 菴羅降居獨洛水，稱第二可汗。

translations.literal: Anluo descended to dwell on the Duluo River and styled himself the Second Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo withdrew to the Duluo River and styled himself the Second Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 大邏便乃請沙缽略曰：「我與爾俱可汗子，各承父後。

translations.literal: Daluobian then petitioned Ishbara, saying: "You and I are both sons of qaghans, each inheriting after our fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian then appealed to Ishbara: "You and I are both sons of qaghans, each heir to our father's line.

sentences.zh: 爾今極尊，我獨無位，何也？」

translations.literal: You now hold the highest honor, while I alone have no position—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: You now hold supreme authority, yet I alone have no rank—why should this be?"

sentences.zh: 沙鉢略患之，以為阿波可汗，還領所部。

translations.literal: Ishbara was troubled by this and made him Apo Qaghan, restoring him to command of his own followers.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara, troubled by the complaint, named him Apo Qaghan and restored him to command of his own followers.

sentences.zh: 沙鉢略勇而得眾，北夷皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Ishbara was brave and won the people's loyalty; all the northern barbarians submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara was bold and won the loyalty of his people, and every northern tribe submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，待之甚薄，北夷大怨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he treated them very poorly, and the northern barbarians were greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, his treatment of the Turks was cold and dismissive, stirring deep resentment among the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 會營州刺史高寶甯作亂，沙缽略與之合軍，攻陷臨渝鎮。

translations.literal: When Gao Baoning, governor of Ying Prefecture, rebelled, Ishbara joined forces with him and captured Linyu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Baoning, governor of Ying Prefecture, rose in rebellion, Ishbara joined his forces and together they captured Linyu Fort.

sentences.zh: 上敕緣邊修保鄣，峻長城，以備之，仍命重將出鎮幽、并。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the border regions to repair fortifications and raise the Great Wall as defense, and dispatched eminent generals to garrison You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered border fortifications repaired and the Great Wall heightened in defense, and dispatched senior generals to garrison You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略妻，宇文氏之女，曰千金公主，自傷宗祀絕滅，每懷復隋之志，日夜言之于沙缽略。

translations.literal: Ishbara's wife was a daughter of the Yuwen clan, called the Princess Qianjin; grieving that her ancestral sacrifices had been extinguished, she constantly harbored the ambition to restore the Zhou and spoke of it day and night to Ishbara.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara's wife was a Yuwen princess known as Princess Qianjin. Grieving the extinction of her dynasty's ancestral rites, she nursed a constant desire to restore Northern Zhou and spoke of it to Ishbara day and night.

sentences.zh: 由是悉衆爲寇，控弦之士四十萬。

translations.literal: On this account he mustered all his forces for raids—four hundred thousand bowmen.
translations.idiomatic: At her urging he mobilized his entire force for raids—four hundred thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 上令柱國馮昱屯乙弗泊，蘭州總管叱李長叉守臨洮，上柱國李崇屯幽州，達奚長儒據周盤，皆爲虜所敗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the pillar of state Feng Yu to encamp at Yifu Marsh, the Lanzhou commander Chilichangcha to hold Linzao, the supreme pillar Li Chong to encamp at Youzhou, and Daxi Changru to hold Zhoupan—all were defeated by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Feng Yu to encamp at Yifu Marsh, Chilichangcha to hold Linzao, Li Chong to garrison Youzhou, and Daxi Changru to defend Zhoupan—but all were defeated by the invaders.

sentences.zh: 於是縱兵自木硤、石門兩道來寇，武威、天水、安定、金城、上郡、弘化、延安六畜鹹盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he unleashed his troops to raid by the Muxia and Shimen routes; livestock in Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shangjun, Honghua, and Yan'an was entirely depleted.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his armies raiding through the Muxia and Shimen passes, stripping Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shangjun, Honghua, and Yan'an of all their livestock.

sentences.zh: 天子震怒，下詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was enraged and issued an edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 往者魏道衰敝，禍難相尋，周、齊抗衡，分割諸夏。

translations.literal: In former times the Wei dynasty declined and weakened; calamities followed one upon another; Zhou and Qi contended for supremacy and partitioned the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Wei dynasty fell into decline, calamities followed in succession, and Northern Zhou and Northern Qi contended for supremacy, carving up the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 突厥之虜，俱通二國。

translations.literal: The Turkic barbarians maintained relations with both states alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks maintained relations with both rival states.

sentences.zh: 周人東慮，恐齊好之深，齊氏西虞，懼周交之厚。

translations.literal: The Zhou people worried in the east, fearing Qi's deep friendship with the Turks; the Qi clan worried in the west, dreading Zhou's close ties with them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou feared in the east that Qi had won the Turks' deepest favor; Northern Qi feared in the west that Zhou had secured the closest ties.

sentences.zh: 謂虜意輕重，國逐安危，非徒並有大敵之憂，思減一邊之防。

translations.literal: They judged the barbarians' favor as the weight that determined each state's safety or peril—not merely sharing the anxiety of a great enemy, but seeking to reduce defenses on one frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Each state judged its safety by where the Turks' favor lay—not merely sharing the burden of a common threat, but scheming to shift the danger onto the rival's border.

sentences.zh: 竭生民之力，供其來往，傾府庫之財，棄于沙漠，華夏之地，實爲勞擾。

translations.literal: They exhausted the people's strength to supply the Turks' comings and goings, poured out treasury wealth to be squandered in the desert—the Central States were truly worn down and harassed.
translations.idiomatic: They exhausted the people's labor to supply the Turks' endless visits, drained their treasuries to feed the desert—the Central Plains were ground down by the burden.

sentences.zh: 猶復劫剝烽戍，殺害吏民，無歲月而不有也。

translations.literal: Yet still they plundered beacon towers and garrison posts and killed officials and commoners—there was scarcely a month or year without such incidents.
translations.idiomatic: And still they raided frontier posts, slaughtered officials and commoners—hardly a month passed without such outrages.

sentences.zh: 惡積禍盈，非止今日。

translations.literal: Evil accumulated and calamity overflowed—this did not begin only today.
translations.idiomatic: Their wickedness has piled up and their doom has ripened—this is no recent development.

sentences.zh: 朕受天明命，子育萬方，湣臣下之勞，除既往之弊。

translations.literal: I have received Heaven's clear mandate and nurture all within the four seas; I pity my subjects' toil and remove the abuses of the past.
translations.idiomatic: Having received Heaven's mandate, I nurture all within the four seas, pity my subjects' suffering, and set out to undo the abuses of the past.

sentences.zh: 以爲厚斂兆庶，多惠豺狼，未嘗感恩，資而爲賊，違天地之意，非帝王之道。

translations.literal: I considered that heavy taxation of the multitude to shower benefits on wolves who never showed gratitude but used the gifts to become bandits violated Heaven and Earth's intent and was not the way of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I judged that taxing the people heavily to shower gifts on wolves who never showed gratitude but turned those gifts against us violated Heaven's intent and was no way for an emperor to rule.

sentences.zh: 節之以禮，不爲虛費，省徭薄賦，國用有餘。

translations.literal: Restraining them with propriety, making no wasteful expenditure, reducing corvée and lightening taxes—the state's resources have surplus.
translations.idiomatic: I have restrained them with proper dignity, refused wasteful expenditure, reduced corvée labor and lightened taxes—and the state's coffers remain full.

sentences.zh: 因入賊之物，加賜將士，息道路之民，務於耕織。

translations.literal: With goods taken from the invaders I have added rewards for officers and soldiers; I have given rest to the people along the roads and set them to farming and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Booty taken from the invaders I have distributed as rewards to my officers and soldiers, while giving the people along the frontier roads respite to devote themselves to farming and weaving.

sentences.zh: 清邊制勝，成策在心。

translations.literal: Securing the borders and achieving victory—the completed strategy is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy for securing the borders and achieving victory is already formed in my mind.

sentences.zh: 凶醜愚暗，未知深旨，將大定之日，比戰國之時，乘昔世之驕，結今時之恨。

translations.literal: These vicious and ugly fools, ignorant and dim, did not understand my deeper intent; taking the day of great pacification to compare with the Warring States period, they rode on past arrogance to forge present hatred.
translations.idiomatic: These brutal fools, blind to my deeper purpose, mistook the day of universal peace for the age of warring states—drawing on old arrogance to stoke new hatred.

sentences.zh: 近者盡其巢窟，俱犯北邊，朕分置軍旅，所在邀截，望其深入，一舉滅之。

translations.literal: Recently they emptied their nests and all invaded the northern border; I have deployed armies in divisions to intercept them wherever they appear, hoping they will penetrate deep so I may destroy them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Recently they emptied their camps and invaded the northern frontier en masse. I have deployed armies at every point to intercept them, hoping they will penetrate deep so that I may destroy them in a single blow.

sentences.zh: 而遠鎮偏師，逢而摧翦，未及南上，遽已奔北，應弦染鍔，過半不歸。

translations.literal: Yet distant garrisons and detached columns encountered and cut them down; before they could push south they had already fled north—those struck by arrows and stained with blades, more than half did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our frontier garrisons and detached columns met and cut them down. Before they could push south they were already fleeing north—more than half of those who fell to arrow and blade never returned home.

sentences.zh: 且彼渠帥，其數凡五，昆季爭長，父叔相猜，外示彌縫，內乖心腹，世行暴虐，家法殘忍。

translations.literal: Moreover, their chieftains number five in all; brothers contend for supremacy, fathers and uncles suspect one another; outwardly they show reconciliation while inwardly their core is divided; generation after generation they practice cruelty, and their household law is savage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their chieftains number five. Brothers vie for supremacy, fathers and uncles suspect one another. Outwardly they show unity while inwardly they are torn apart. Generation after generation they have ruled through cruelty, and their own household law is savage.

sentences.zh: 東夷諸國，盡挾私仇，西戎群長，皆有宿怨。

translations.literal: All the eastern barbarian states harbor private grudges; all the western Rong chieftains bear old enmities.
translations.idiomatic: Every eastern tribe nurses a private grudge against them; every western chieftain harbors an old grievance.

sentences.zh: 突厥之北，契丹之徒，切齒磨牙，常伺其便。

translations.literal: North of the Turks, the Khitan and their kind gnash their teeth and grind their jaws, constantly watching for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, the Khitan and their kin gnash their teeth, ever watching for an opening.

sentences.zh: 達頭前攻酒泉，其後于闐、波斯、挹怛三國一時即叛。

translations.literal: Tardu previously attacked Jiuquan; afterward Khotan, Persia, and the Yeda all rebelled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu had previously attacked Jiuquan, and afterward Khotan, Persia, and the Yeda all rebelled at the same time.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略近趣周盤，其部內薄孤、束紇羅尋亦翻動。

translations.literal: Ishbara recently pressed toward Zhoupan; within his domain Bogu and Shuheluo soon also rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara had recently pressed toward Zhoupan, and within his own domain Bogu and Shuheluo soon rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 往年利稽察大爲高麗、靺鞨所破，娑毗設又爲紇支可汗所殺。

translations.literal: In former years Lijicha was greatly defeated by Goguryeo and the Mohe; Suobishe was also killed by Hezhi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years Lijicha was crushed by Goguryeo and the Mohe, and Suobishe was killed by Hezhi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 與其爲鄰，皆願誅剿。

translations.literal: All who border them wish to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Every neighbor wishes to see them destroyed.

sentences.zh: 部落之下，盡異純民，千種萬類，仇敵怨偶，泣血拊心，銜悲積恨。

translations.literal: Beneath the tribes are all diverse peoples of mixed stock—thousands of kinds and myriad categories, enemies and aggrieved parties, weeping blood and beating their breasts, bearing grief and accumulated hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath their rule live peoples of countless origins—thousands of tribes, myriad grudges, enemies and wronged parties who weep blood and beat their breasts, nursing grief and accumulated hatred.

sentences.zh: 圓首方足，皆人類也，有一於此，更切朕懷。

translations.literal: Round-headed and square-footed, all are human beings; that any one of these conditions exists cuts more deeply into my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Round of head and square of foot—they are human beings all. That any of this should be so weighs all the more heavily on my heart.

sentences.zh: 彼地咎徵妖作，年將一紀，乃獸爲人語，人作神言，云其國亡，訖而不見。

translations.literal: In their lands ominous portents and demonic manifestations have occurred for nearly twelve years—beasts speaking with human voices, men uttering divine words, proclaiming their state's destruction, then vanishing without trace.
translations.idiomatic: In their lands ominous portents and supernatural disturbances have persisted for nearly twelve years—beasts speaking with human voices, men uttering prophecies of their nation's fall, then vanishing without a trace.

sentences.zh: 每冬雷震，觸地火生，種類資給，惟藉水草。

translations.literal: Every winter thunder resounds, fire springs from the ground when touched; their sustenance depends solely on water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: Every winter brings thunder, and fire springs from the ground at a touch. Their livelihood depends entirely on pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 去歲四時，竟無雨雪，川枯蝗暴，卉木燒盡，饑疫死亡，人畜相半。

translations.literal: Last year through all four seasons there was no rain or snow; rivers dried up and locusts swarmed; vegetation was burned away; famine and pestilence brought death—men and livestock perished by half.
translations.idiomatic: Last year brought no rain or snow through all four seasons. Rivers ran dry, locusts swarmed, vegetation withered, and famine and pestilence killed half their people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 舊居之所，赤地無依，遷徙漠南，偷存晷刻。

translations.literal: Their old dwelling places are bare earth with nothing to depend on; they have migrated south of the desert, stealing moments of survival.
translations.idiomatic: Their old pastures lie barren and desolate. They have migrated south of the desert, clinging to life moment by moment.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋上天所忿，驅就齊斧，幽明合契，今也其時。

translations.literal: Surely this is Heaven's wrath, driving them toward the executioner's block; the hidden and manifest are in accord—the time is now.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Heaven itself is enraged, driving them toward the executioner's block. The signs from above and below are aligned—the time has come.

sentences.zh: 故選將治兵，贏糧聚甲，義士奮發，壯夫肆憤，願取名王之首，思撻單于之背，雲歸霧集，不可數也。

translations.literal: Therefore I have selected generals, trained troops, loaded provisions and gathered armor; men of righteousness rise in ardor, stalwart warriors unleash their fury, eager to take the heads of barbarian kings and lash the backs of chanyu—gathering like clouds and mists, they cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore chosen my generals, trained my armies, stockpiled provisions and armor. Righteous men rise in ardor, stalwart warriors unleash their fury, eager to claim the heads of barbarian kings and lash the backs of chanyu—they gather like clouds and mist, beyond all counting.

sentences.zh: 東極滄海，西盡流沙，縱百勝之兵，橫萬里之衆，亙朔野之追躡，望天崖而一掃。

translations.literal: East to the eastern sea, west to the flowing sands—unleashing an army victorious a hundred times, deploying forces spanning ten thousand li, pursuing across the northern wilds, sweeping clean to the horizon.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern sea to the western sands, with an army undefeated in a hundred battles and forces stretching ten thousand li, we shall pursue them across the northern steppe and sweep them clean to the horizon.

sentences.zh: 此則王恢所說，其猶射癰，何敵能當，何遠不服！

translations.literal: This is what Wang Hui spoke of—it is like lancing an abscess; what enemy can withstand it, what distant land will not submit!
translations.idiomatic: This is what Wang Hui meant—it is like lancing an abscess. What enemy can stand against us? What distant land will not submit!

sentences.zh: 但皇王舊跡，北止幽都，荒遐之表，文軌所棄。

translations.literal: But the ancient traces of emperors and kings stopped at Youdu in the north; beyond the remote wilderness lies territory abandoned by civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancient domain of emperors and kings extended north only to Youdu. Beyond the remote wilderness lies land that civilization itself has abandoned.

sentences.zh: 得其地不可而居，得其民不忍皆殺，無勞兵革，遠規溟海。

translations.literal: Gaining their land, one cannot dwell there; gaining their people, one cannot bear to kill them all. There is no need for arms and armor, nor to scheme as far as the distant sea.
translations.idiomatic: Their land cannot be settled; their people cannot all be slaughtered. There is no need for arms and armor, nor to extend our ambitions to the distant sea.

sentences.zh: 諸將今行，義兼含育，有降者納，有違者死。

translations.literal: Generals, in this campaign your duty combines nurture with restraint: those who surrender shall be received; those who resist shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, in this campaign your duty is both to nurture and to restrain: accept those who surrender; put to death those who resist.

sentences.zh: 異域殊方，被其擁抑，放聽復舊。

translations.literal: Peoples of foreign lands and distant regions oppressed by them—release them and allow them to return to their former ways.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples of foreign lands oppressed by the Turks—release them and allow them to return to their former ways.

sentences.zh: 廣辟邊境，嚴治關塞，使其不敢南望，永服威刑。

translations.literal: Broaden the frontier borders and strictly govern the passes, so that they dare not look south and forever submit to awe and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Broaden our frontier defenses and strictly govern the passes, so that they dare not look south and forever submit to our authority.

sentences.zh: 臥鼓息烽，暫勞終逸，制禦夷狄，義在斯乎！

translations.literal: Lay down drums and extinguish beacon fires—temporary toil for lasting ease; to control and restrain the barbarians, is not the purpose here!
translations.idiomatic: Lay down drums and extinguish beacon fires—temporary toil for lasting peace. To control and restrain the barbarians—this is the purpose!

sentences.zh: 何用侍子之朝，甯勞渭橋之拜。

translations.literal: Why need the attendance of hostages at court, or trouble oneself with bows at Wei Bridge?
translations.idiomatic: Why require hostages at court, or trouble ourselves with ceremonial bows at Wei Bridge?

sentences.zh: 普告海內，知朕意焉。

translations.literal: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm, so all may know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm, so all may know my intent.

sentences.zh: 於是以河間王弘、上柱國豆盧勣、竇榮定、左僕射高熲、右僕射虞慶則並爲元帥，出塞擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Hong of Hejian, the supreme pillar Dou Luqi, Dou Rongding, Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, and Right Vice Director Yu Qingze were all made commanders-in-chief and marched beyond the frontier to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince Hong of Hejian, the supreme pillar Dou Luqi, Dou Rongding, Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, and Right Vice Director Yu Qingze as commanders-in-chief and sent them beyond the frontier to attack the Turks.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略率阿波、貪汗二可汗等來拒戰，皆敗走遁去。

translations.literal: Ishbara led Apo Qaghan, Tanhan Qaghan, and others to resist in battle; all were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara led Apo Qaghan, Tanhan Qaghan, and others to resist, but all were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 時虜饑甚，不能得食，於是粉骨爲糧，又多災疫，死者極衆。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians were extremely hungry and could obtain no food; they ground bones into meal for sustenance, and pestilence also spread—dead were exceedingly many.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were starving and could find no food, grinding bones into meal to survive. Pestilence swept through their camps, and the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 既而沙缽略以阿波驍悍，忌之，因其先歸，襲擊其部，大破之，殺阿波之母。

translations.literal: Then Ishbara, because Apo was fierce and formidable, envied him; taking advantage of his early return, he raided Apo's followers, routed them utterly, and killed Apo's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara, envying Apo's martial prowess, took advantage of his early return to raid his followers, crushing them and killing Apo's mother.

sentences.zh: 阿波還無所歸，西奔達頭可汗。

translations.literal: Apo returned with nowhere to go and fled west to Tardu Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Apo returned to find himself homeless and fled west to Tardu Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 達頭者，名玷厥，沙缽略之從父也，舊爲西面可汗。

translations.literal: Tardu was named Dianjue, Ishbara's paternal uncle, formerly the Western Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu, whose personal name was Dianjue, was Ishbara's paternal uncle and had formerly been the Western Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 既而大怒，遣阿波率兵而東，各落歸之者將十萬騎，遂與沙缽略相攻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was greatly angered and sent Apo east with troops; tribes returning to him numbered nearly one hundred thousand horsemen, and they attacked Ishbara.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tardu sent Apo east with an army. Nearly one hundred thousand horsemen from various tribes rallied to him, and they attacked Ishbara.

sentences.zh: 又有貪汗可汗，素睦于阿波，沙缽略奪其衆而廢之，貪汗亡奔達頭。

translations.literal: There was also Tanhan Qaghan, who had always been on good terms with Apo; Ishbara seized his followers and deposed him, and Tanhan fled to Tardu.
translations.idiomatic: Tanhan Qaghan, who had always been allied with Apo, had his followers seized and was deposed by Ishbara. He fled to Tardu.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略從弟地勤察別統部落，與沙缽略有隙，復以衆叛歸阿波。

translations.literal: Ishbara's younger cousin Diliqiecha separately commanded a tribe; having a rift with Ishbara, he again rebelled with his followers and joined Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara's younger cousin Diliqiecha, who commanded a separate tribe and had fallen out with Ishbara, rebelled with his followers and joined Apo.

sentences.zh: 連兵不已，各遣使詣闕，請和求援，上皆不許。

translations.literal: Fighting continued without cease; each side sent envoys to the court seeking peace and aid, but the emperor refused all.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued without cease. Each side sent envoys to the Sui court seeking peace and aid, but the emperor refused them all.

sentences.zh: 會千金公主上書，請爲一子之例，高祖遣開府徐平和使于沙缽略。

translations.literal: When Princess Qianjin submitted a memorial requesting the arrangement of a son-in-law, Emperor Gaozu dispatched the palace gate commander Xu Pinghe as envoy to Ishbara.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin submitted a memorial requesting that the relationship be formalized as that of father-in-law and son. Emperor Gaozu dispatched Xu Pinghe as envoy to Ishbara.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣時鎮并州，請因其釁而乘之，上不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was then garrisoning Bingzhou and requested to take advantage of the rift to strike; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang, then garrisoning Bingzhou, asked permission to strike while the Turks were divided. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略遣使致書曰：「辰年九月十日，從天生大突厥天下賢聖天子伊利俱盧設莫何始波羅可汗致書大隋皇帝：使人開府徐平和至，辱告言語，具聞也。

translations.literal: Ishbara sent an envoy with a letter, saying: "On the tenth day of the ninth month of the Chen year, the Heaven-born Great Turkic All-under-Heaven Sage Son of Heaven Illi Gul Shemohe Shiboluo Qaghan writes to the Great Sui Emperor: Your envoy, the palace gate commander Xu Pinghe, has arrived; I am honored by your message and have heard it all.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara sent a letter reading: "On the tenth day of the ninth month of the Chen year, the Heaven-born Great Turkic Sage Son of Heaven Illi Gul Shemohe Shiboluo Qaghan writes to the Great Sui Emperor: Your envoy, Palace-Opener Xu Pinghe, has arrived. I am honored by your message and have heard it in full.

sentences.zh: 皇帝是婦父，即是翁，此是女夫，即是兒例。

translations.literal: The Emperor is my wife's father, which is to say my father-in-law; I am my wife's husband, which is to say a son in relation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is my wife's father—that is, my father-in-law. I am my wife's husband—that is, a son to him.

sentences.zh: 兩境雖殊，情義是一。

translations.literal: Though our two realms differ, our affection and duty are one.
translations.idiomatic: Though our two realms differ, our bond of affection and duty is one.

sentences.zh: 今重疊親舊，子子孫孫，乃至萬世不斷，上天爲證，終不違負。

translations.literal: Now with layered ties of kinship, from sons to grandsons, unbroken even unto ten thousand generations—Heaven as witness, I shall never betray this bond.
translations.idiomatic: With these ties of kinship binding sons and grandsons for ten thousand generations, Heaven is my witness—I shall never betray this bond.

sentences.zh: 此國所有羊馬，都是皇帝畜生，彼有繒彩，都是此物，彼此有何異也！」

translations.literal: All the sheep and horses in this realm belong to the Emperor's livestock; the silks and brocades there are all the same goods—what difference is there between us!
translations.idiomatic: All the sheep and horses in my realm belong to the Emperor. The silks and brocades in yours are the same goods—what difference is there between us!"

sentences.zh: 高祖報書曰：「大隋天子貽書大突厥伊利俱盧設莫何沙缽略可汗：得書，知大有好心向此也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu replied: "The Great Sui Son of Heaven sends this letter to the Great Turkic Illi Gul Shemohe Ishbara Qaghan: Having received your letter, I know you harbor good will toward us.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu replied: "The Great Sui Son of Heaven sends this letter to the Great Turkic Illi Gul Shemohe Ishbara Qaghan: I have received your letter and know you harbor good will toward us.

sentences.zh: 既是沙缽略婦翁，今日看沙缽略共兒子不異。

translations.literal: Since I am Ishbara's father-in-law, today I regard Ishbara no differently from a son.
translations.idiomatic: As Ishbara's father-in-law, I regard him today no differently than a son.

sentences.zh: 既以親舊厚意，常使之外，今特別遣大臣虞慶則往彼看女，復看沙缽略也。」

translations.literal: Having always sent envoys out of affection for our kinship, now I specially dispatch the great minister Yu Qingze to go there to see my daughter and also to see Ishbara."
translations.idiomatic: I have always sent envoys out of affection for our kinship. Now I specially dispatch the great minister Yu Qingze to visit my daughter and also to see Ishbara."

sentences.zh: 沙缽略陳兵，列其寶物，坐見慶則，稱病不能起，且曰：「我父伯以來，不向人拜。」

translations.literal: Ishbara deployed troops, displayed his treasures, and received Qingze seated, claiming illness and inability to rise, saying: "Since my fathers and uncles, we have never bowed to anyone."
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara deployed his troops, displayed his treasures, and received Qingze while seated, claiming illness and refusing to rise. He said: "Since the time of my fathers and uncles, we have never bowed to anyone."

sentences.zh: 慶則責而喻之。

translations.literal: Qingze rebuked him and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze rebuked him and made his duty clear.

sentences.zh: 千金公主私謂慶則曰：「可汗豺狼性，過與爭，將齧人。」

translations.literal: Princess Qianjin privately told Qingze: "The qaghan has the nature of a wolf; if you press him too hard, he will bite.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin privately warned Qingze: "The qaghan has the nature of a wolf. Press him too hard and he will bite."

sentences.zh: 長孫晟說諭之，攝圖辭屈，乃頓顙跪受璽書，以戴於首。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Sheng persuaded and instructed him; Shetu's arguments were exhausted, and he prostrated himself kneeling to receive the imperial letter, placing it on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng persuaded him further. With his arguments exhausted, Shetu prostrated himself and knelt to receive the imperial letter, placing it on his head.

sentences.zh: 既而大慚，其羣下因相聚慟哭。

translations.literal: Afterward he was deeply ashamed, and his followers gathered together and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply ashamed, he and his followers gathered together and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 慶則又遣稱臣，沙鉢略謂其屬曰：「何名為臣？」

translations.literal: Qingze further had him styled a subject; Ishbara said to his followers: "What is meant by being a subject?
translations.idiomatic: Qingze further had him styled a subject. Ishbara asked his followers: "What does it mean to be a subject?"

sentences.zh: 報曰：「隋國稱臣，猶此稱奴耳。」

translations.literal: They replied: "To be a subject of Sui is the same as being called a slave here."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "To be a subject of Sui is the same as being called a slave among us."

sentences.zh: 沙缽略曰：「得作大隋天子奴，虞僕射之力也。」

translations.literal: Ishbara said: "That I can be a slave of the Great Sui Son of Heaven is thanks to Vice Director Yu's efforts."
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara said: "That I am now a slave of the Great Sui Son of Heaven is thanks to Vice Director Yu."

sentences.zh: 贈慶則馬千匹，並以從妹妻之。

translations.literal: He presented Qingze with a thousand horses and gave him a younger cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He presented Qingze with a thousand horses and gave him a younger cousin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時沙缽略既爲達頭所困，又東畏契丹，遣使告急，請將部落度漠南，寄居白道川內，有詔許之。

translations.literal: At that time Ishbara, beset by Tardu and also fearing the Khitan in the east, sent envoys in urgent appeal, requesting to lead his tribe south across the desert to dwell within the White Road River valley; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: Beset by Tardu and fearing the Khitan in the east, Ishbara sent an urgent appeal requesting to lead his tribe south across the desert to settle in the White Road River valley. An edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 詔晉王廣以兵援之，給以衣食，賜以車服鼓吹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Jin Guang to aid him with troops, provide food and clothing, and bestow carriages, robes, and musical ensembles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince of Jin Yang Guang to aid him with troops, provide food and clothing, and bestow carriages, robes, and a ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略因西擊阿波，破擒之。

translations.literal: Ishbara thereupon attacked Apo in the west, defeated and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara then attacked Apo in the west, defeated him, and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 而阿拔國部落乘虛掠其妻子。

translations.literal: But the Aba tribe took advantage of the opening to plunder his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Aba tribe took advantage of the opening to plunder his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 官軍爲擊阿拔，敗之，所獲悉與沙缽略。

translations.literal: Government troops attacked the Aba and defeated them; all that was captured was given entirely to Ishbara.
translations.idiomatic: Sui troops attacked the Aba and defeated them, giving all that was captured to Ishbara.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大喜，乃立約，以磧爲界，因上表曰：

translations.literal: Ishbara was greatly pleased; they established a treaty with the desert as boundary, and he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased, Ishbara established a treaty with the desert as the boundary and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 大突厥伊利俱盧設始波羅莫何可汗臣攝圖言：大使尚書右僕射虞慶則至，伏奉詔書，兼宣慈旨，仰惟恩信之著，逾久愈明，徒知負荷，不能答謝。

translations.literal: The Great Turkic Illi Gul Sheboluo Mohe Qaghan, subject Shetu, states: The great envoy, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Qingze, has arrived; I humbly received the imperial edict and also heard the benevolent intent. Reflecting on the manifest grace and trust, the longer it endures the clearer it becomes; I can only bear this burden and cannot adequately give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Turkic Illi Gul Sheboluo Mohe Qaghan, your subject Shetu, respectfully states: Your great envoy, Right Vice Director Yu Qingze, has arrived bearing your edict and benevolent intent. Your grace and trust grow clearer with each passing day. I can only bear this burden and cannot adequately express my gratitude.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大隋皇帝之有四海，上契天心，下順民望，二儀之所覆載，七曜之所照臨，莫不委質來賓，回首面內。

translations.literal: Reflecting that the Great Sui Emperor possesses the four seas, matching Heaven's heart above and following the people's hopes below—all covered and borne by the two principles, all illuminated by the seven luminaries—none fail to submit their substance and come as guests, turning back to face inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Sui Emperor holds the four seas, matching Heaven's will above and the people's hopes below. All beneath the sky and sun, all illuminated by the seven luminaries, submit their allegiance and turn toward your court.

sentences.zh: 實萬世之一聖，千年之一期，求之古昔，未始聞也。

translations.literal: Truly a sage of ten thousand generations, an era of a thousand years—seeking in antiquity, this has never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: You are truly a sage of ten thousand generations, an era come once in a thousand years—unprecedented in all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 突厥自天置以來，五十余載，保有沙漠，自王蕃隅。

translations.literal: The Turks, since Heaven established them, for more than fifty years have held the desert and ruled their own borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, since Heaven established them more than fifty years ago, have held the desert and ruled their own borderlands.

sentences.zh: 地過萬里，士馬億數，恆力兼戎夷，抗禮華夏，在於北狄，莫與爲大。

translations.literal: Their territory spans more than ten thousand li, their warriors and horses number in the hundreds of millions; constantly their strength matched both Rong and Yi, they treated the Central States as equals—in the northern barbarians, none was greater.
translations.idiomatic: Our territory spans more than ten thousand li, our warriors and horses number in the hundreds of millions. We long matched our strength against all the frontier tribes and treated the Central States as equals. Among the northern peoples, none was greater.

sentences.zh: 頃者氣候清和，風雲順序，意以華夏其有大聖興焉。

translations.literal: Recently the climate has been clear and harmonious, winds and clouds in proper order—I understood that in the Central States a great sage would arise.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the climate has been clear and harmonious, winds and clouds in proper order—I understood that a great sage would arise in the Central States.

sentences.zh: 況今被沾德義，仁化所及，禮讓之風，自朝滿野。

translations.literal: Moreover, now having been touched by virtue and righteousness, where benevolent transformation reaches, the wind of courtesy and yielding fills the court and spreads to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Now having been touched by your virtue and righteousness, the spirit of courtesy and yielding fills your court and spreads across the land.

sentences.zh: 竊以天無二日，土無二王，伏惟大隋皇帝，真皇帝也。

translations.literal: I consider that Heaven has no two suns, the earth has no two kings—reflecting, the Great Sui Emperor is the true emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has no two suns; the earth has no two kings. The Great Sui Emperor is the true emperor.

sentences.zh: 豈敢阻兵恃險，偷竊名號，今便感慕淳風，歸心有道，屈膝稽顙，永爲籓附。

translations.literal: How would I dare to rely on arms and terrain, stealthily usurping titles? Now I am moved by the pure wind, my heart turns to the Way; bending knee and knocking forehead, I shall forever be a frontier subject.
translations.idiomatic: How would I dare to rely on arms and terrain, stealthily usurping titles? Now, moved by your pure governance, my heart turns to the Way. Bending knee and knocking forehead, I shall forever be your frontier subject.

sentences.zh: 雖復南瞻魏闕，山川悠遠，北面之禮，不敢廢失。

translations.literal: Though gazing south toward the Wei palace gate across distant mountains and rivers, the rites of facing north I dare not neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Though your palace lies far to the south across distant mountains and rivers, I dare not neglect the rites of facing north in submission.

sentences.zh: 當令侍子入朝，神馬歲貢，朝夕恭承，唯命是視。

translations.literal: I shall have an attendant son enter court, present divine horses as annual tribute, respectfully receive commands morning and evening, and look only to your orders.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth I shall send my son to court, present divine horses as annual tribute, and respectfully await your commands morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 至於削衽解辮，革音從律，習俗已久，未能改變。

translations.literal: As for cutting the lapel, unbraiding hair, and changing speech to follow standards—these customs are long established and cannot yet be changed.
translations.idiomatic: As for cutting our lapels, unbraiding our hair, and changing our speech to follow your standards—these customs are long established and cannot yet be changed.

sentences.zh: 闔國同心，無不銜荷，不任下情欣慕之至。

translations.literal: The whole realm is of one heart; none fail to bear this grace. I cannot contain the fullness of my joy and admiration below.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm is of one heart; none fail to bear your grace. I cannot contain the fullness of my joy and admiration.

sentences.zh: 謹遣第七兒臣窟含真等奉表以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully I dispatch my seventh son, subject Kuhanzhen, and others to present this memorial for your knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I dispatch my seventh son Kuhanzhen and others to present this memorial.

sentences.zh: 高祖下詔曰：「沙缽略稱雄漠北，多曆世年，百蠻之大，莫過於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "Ishbara has held sway north of the desert for many generations; among the hundred barbarians, none is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "Ishbara has held sway north of the desert for many generations. Among the hundred barbarian peoples, none is greater.

sentences.zh: 往雖與和，猶是二國，今作君臣，便成一體。

translations.literal: Formerly though at peace, we were still two states; now as lord and subject, we have become one body.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, though at peace, we were still two states. Now, as lord and subject, we have become one.

sentences.zh: 情深義厚，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The affection is deep and the duty thick—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: The bond is deep and the duty sincere—I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 荷天之休，海外有截，豈朕薄德所能致此！

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven's blessing, beyond the seas all is orderly—how could my meager virtue bring this about!
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Heaven's blessing, all beyond the seas is at peace—how could my meager virtue alone bring this about!

sentences.zh: 已敕有司肅告郊廟，宜普頒天下，咸使知聞。」

translations.literal: I have ordered the officials to solemnly announce this at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; it should be broadly promulgated throughout the realm so all may know.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered the officials to announce this solemnly at the suburban altars and ancestral temples. Let it be promulgated throughout the realm so all may know."

sentences.zh: 自是詔答諸事並不稱其名以異之。

translations.literal: From this time, in edicts and replies on all matters his name was not used, to mark him as distinct.
translations.idiomatic: From this time, edicts and replies addressed to him no longer used his personal name, marking his special status.

sentences.zh: 其妻可賀敦，周千金公主，賜姓楊氏，編之屬籍，改封大義公主。

translations.literal: His wife Kehedun, the Zhou Princess Qianjin, was granted the surname Yang, enrolled in the imperial clan register, and re-enfeoffed as Princess Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Kehedun, the former Zhou Princess Qianjin, was granted the surname Yang, enrolled in the imperial clan register, and re-enfeoffed as Princess Dayi.

sentences.zh: 策拜窟含真爲柱國，封安國公，宴於內殿，引見皇后，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: By imperial decree Kuhanzhen was appointed pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo; he was feasted in the inner hall, introduced to the empress, and rewarded most generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kuhanzhen was appointed pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo. He was feasted in the inner hall, introduced to the empress, and rewarded most generously.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大悅，於是歲時貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Ishbara was greatly pleased, and from then on tribute was sent without cease through the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara was greatly pleased, and from then on sent tribute without cease through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，沙缽略遣其子入貢方物，因請獵於恆、代之間，又許之，仍遣人賜其酒食。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Ishbara sent his son to present tribute goods and requested to hunt between Heng and Dai; this was again permitted, and envoys were sent bearing wine and food as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, Ishbara sent his son to present tribute and requested permission to hunt between Heng and Dai. Permission was granted, and envoys were sent bearing wine and food.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略率部落再拜受賜。

translations.literal: Ishbara led his tribe in double prostration to receive the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara led his tribe in double prostration to receive the gifts.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略一日手殺鹿十八頭，齎尾舌以獻。

translations.literal: Ishbara personally killed eighteen deer in one day and presented their tails and tongues as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara personally killed eighteen deer in a single day and presented their tails and tongues as tribute.

sentences.zh: 還至紫河鎮，其牙帳爲火所燒，沙缽略惡之，月餘而卒。

translations.literal: Returning to Zihe Fort, his headquarters tent was burned by fire; Ishbara took this as an ill omen and died a little over a month later.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Zihe Fort, his headquarters tent was consumed by fire. Ishbara took this as an ill omen and died a little over a month later.

sentences.zh: 上爲廢朝三日，遣太常弔祭焉。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for three days and dispatched the Minister of Ceremonies to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for three days and dispatched the Minister of Ceremonies to offer condolences and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 贈物五千段。

translations.literal: Five thousand bolts of goods were sent as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand bolts of goods were sent as gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，攝圖以其子雍虞閭性芃，遺令立其弟葉護處羅侯；

translations.literal: Initially, Shetu, because his son Yudoulu was weak in character, left instructions to install his younger brother Yehu Chuluohou;
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Shetu, finding his son Yudoulu weak in character, left instructions to install his younger brother Yehu Chuluohou as qaghan;

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭遣使迎處羅侯，將立之。

translations.literal: Yudoulu sent envoys to welcome Chuluohou, intending to install him.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu sent envoys to welcome Chuluohou, intending to install him as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 處羅侯曰：「我突厥自木杆可汗以來，多以弟代兄，以庶奪嫡，失先祖之法，不相敬畏。

translations.literal: Chuluohou said: "Our Turks, since Mughan Qaghan, have often replaced elder brothers with younger ones, usurped legitimate heirs with lesser sons, losing the law of our ancestors and failing to respect one another.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou said: "Since Mughan Qaghan, our Turks have often replaced elder brothers with younger ones and usurped legitimate heirs with lesser sons, abandoning the law of our ancestors and losing all mutual respect.

sentences.zh: 汝當嗣位，我不憚拜汝也。」

translations.literal: You should succeed to the throne; I do not shrink from bowing to you.
translations.idiomatic: You should succeed to the throne. I do not shrink from bowing to you."

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭又遣使謂處羅侯曰：「叔與我父，共根連體，我是枝葉。

translations.literal: Yudoulu again sent envoys to tell Chuluohou: "Uncle and my father share one root and connected body; I am the branch and leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu sent envoys to tell Chuluohou: "Uncle and my father share one root and one body. I am but the branch and leaf.

sentences.zh: 甯有我作主，令根本反同枝葉，令叔父之尊下我卑稚！

translations.literal: How could I be master and make the root become like the branch and leaf, making my uncle's honored status bow to my lowly youth!
translations.idiomatic: How could I take the throne and make the root become like the branch, placing my uncle's honored status beneath my lowly youth!

sentences.zh: 又亡父之命，其可廢乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, my deceased father's command—how can it be set aside!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, how can I set aside my deceased father's command!

sentences.zh: 願叔勿疑。」

translations.literal: I pray uncle, do not doubt."
translations.idiomatic: I pray you, uncle, do not doubt."

sentences.zh: 相讓者五六，處羅侯竟立，是爲葉護可汗。

translations.literal: They yielded to each other five or six times; in the end Chuluohou was installed, becoming Yehu Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded to each other five or six times. In the end Chuluohou was installed as Yehu Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 以雍虞閭爲葉護。

translations.literal: Yudoulu was made Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu was appointed Yehu.

sentences.zh: 遣使上表言狀，上賜之鼓吹幡旗。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to submit a memorial reporting the situation; the emperor bestowed upon him musical ensembles, banners, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to report the situation. The emperor bestowed upon him musical ensembles, banners, and flags.

sentences.zh: 處羅侯長頤僂背，眉目疏朗，勇而有謀，以隋所賜旗鼓西征阿波。

translations.literal: Chuluohou had a long neck and stooped back, sparse but clear features, was brave and resourceful; with the banners and drums bestowed by Sui he marched west against Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou had a long neck and stooped back, with sparse but clear features. Brave and resourceful, he marched west against Apo bearing the banners and drums bestowed by Sui.

sentences.zh: 敵人以爲得隋兵所助，多來降附，遂生擒阿波。

translations.literal: The enemy thought he had received aid from Sui troops; many came to surrender and submit, and he captured Apo alive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy believed he had Sui troops at his back. Many surrendered to him, and he captured Apo alive.

sentences.zh: 既而上書請阿波死生之命，上下其議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting decision on Apo's life or death, and the matter was referred for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial requesting a decision on Apo's life or death, and the matter was referred for discussion at court.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲進曰：「骨肉相殘，教之蠹也。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong advanced and said: "Kin slaughtering kin—this is the bane of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong said: "Kin slaughtering kin—this is the bane of good governance.

sentences.zh: 存養以示寬大。」

translations.literal: Spare and nurture him to show magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Spare him and let him live, to show magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Good."

sentences.zh: 熲因奉觴進曰：「自軒轅以來，獯粥多爲邊患。

translations.literal: Jiong thereupon raised a cup and advanced, saying: "Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Xunyu have often been a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong raised a cup and said: "Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the Xiongnu have been a constant frontier menace.

sentences.zh: 今遠窮北海，皆爲臣妾，此之盛事，振古未聞，臣敢再拜上壽。」

translations.literal: Now driven far to the ends of the northern sea, all have become subjects and servants—this glorious event, unprecedented since antiquity; your subject dares bow twice and offer congratulations on your longevity."
translations.idiomatic: Now driven to the ends of the northern sea, all have become your subjects—an achievement unprecedented since antiquity. Your servant dares bow twice and offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 其後處羅侯又西征，中流矢而卒，其衆奉雍虞閭爲主，是爲頡伽施多那都藍可汗。

translations.literal: Afterward Chuluohou again marched west, was struck by an arrow midstream and died; his followers installed Yudoulu as leader, who became Jiagashiduona Dulü Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou later marched west again, was struck by an arrow, and died. His followers installed Yudoulu as leader, who became Jiagashiduona Dulü Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭遣使詣闕，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: Yudoulu sent envoys to the court and was granted three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu sent envoys to court and was granted three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 每歲遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Each year he sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 時有流人楊欽亡入突厥中，謬云彭國公劉昶與宇文氏謀反，令大義公主發兵擾邊。

translations.literal: At that time the exile Yang Qin fled into the Turks and falsely claimed that Liu Chang, Duke of Peng, was plotting rebellion with the Yuwen clan, ordering Princess Dayi to raise troops and harass the border.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the exile Yang Qin fled to the Turks and falsely claimed that Liu Chang, Duke of Peng, was plotting rebellion with the Yuwen clan, and that Princess Dayi had been ordered to raise troops and harass the border.

sentences.zh: 都藍執欽以聞，並貢葧布、魚膠。

translations.literal: Dulü seized Qin and reported this, and also presented tribute of hemp cloth and fish glue.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü seized Qin and reported the matter, and also presented tribute of hemp cloth and fish glue.

sentences.zh: 其弟欽羽設部落強盛，都藍忌而擊之，斬首於陣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qinyushe's tribe was powerful; Dulü envied and attacked him, beheading him on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qinyushe commanded a powerful tribe. Envying his strength, Dulü attacked and beheaded him on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 其年，遣其母弟褥但特勤獻於闐玉杖，上拜褥但爲柱國、康國公。

translations.literal: That year he sent his younger maternal brother Rutan Teqin to present a Khotan jade staff; the emperor appointed Rutan as pillar of state and Duke of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sent his younger maternal brother Rutan Teqin to present a Khotan jade staff. The emperor appointed Rutan as pillar of state and Duke of Kang.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥部落大人相率遣使貢馬萬匹，羊二萬口，駝、牛各五百頭。

translations.literal: The following year, the great chiefs of the Turkic tribes together sent envoys presenting ten thousand horses, twenty thousand sheep, and five hundred each of camels and cattle as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the great chiefs of the Turkic tribes together sent envoys presenting ten thousand horses, twenty thousand sheep, and five hundred camels and cattle each as tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使請緣邊置市，與中國貿易，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon they sent envoys requesting border markets for trade with the Central States; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: They soon sent envoys requesting border markets for trade with China. An edict granted their request.

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，上以陳叔寶屏風賜大義公主，主心恆不平，因書屏風爲詩，敘陳亡自寄。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, the emperor bestowed upon Princess Dayi the screen of Chen Shubao; the princess's heart was always unsettled, and she wrote a poem on the screen, narrating Chen's fall to express her own feelings.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, the emperor bestowed Chen Shubao's screen upon Princess Dayi. Her heart was never at peace, and she wrote a poem on the screen lamenting Chen's fall and expressing her own sorrow.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：「盛衰等朝暮，世道若浮萍。

translations.literal: The words read: "Rise and fall are like morning and evening; the ways of the world are like duckweed adrift.
translations.idiomatic: The poem read: "Rise and fall are like morning and evening; the ways of the world drift like duckweed.

sentences.zh: 榮華實難守，池台終自平。

translations.literal: Glory and splendor are truly hard to keep; ponds and terraces in the end level themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Glory and splendor are hard to hold; ponds and terraces in the end return to level ground.

sentences.zh: 富貴今何在？

translations.literal: Where is wealth and nobility now?
translations.idiomatic: Where is wealth and nobility now?

sentences.zh: 空事寫丹青。

translations.literal: In vain they are painted in colors.
translations.idiomatic: They survive only as painted images.

sentences.zh: 杯酒恆無樂，弦歌詎有聲！

translations.literal: Wine cups bring no lasting joy; how can string and song have sound!
translations.idiomatic: Wine cups bring no lasting joy; how can string and song have sound!

sentences.zh: 余本皇家子，飄流入虜庭。

translations.literal: I was originally a child of the imperial house, adrift and washed into the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: I was born a child of the imperial house, yet drifted into the barbarian court.

sentences.zh: 一朝睹成敗，懷抱忽縱橫。

translations.literal: One morning witnessing success and failure, my bosom suddenly overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: One morning, witnessing rise and fall, my heart overflowed with grief.

sentences.zh: 古來共如此，非我獨申名。

translations.literal: Since antiquity it has always been thus—not I alone who speak this name.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity it has always been thus—I am not alone in my fate.

sentences.zh: 唯有《明君曲》，偏傷遠嫁情。」

translations.literal: Only the 'Song of the Bright Lord' especially wounds the feelings of one far-married.
translations.idiomatic: Only the 'Song of the Bright Lord' especially wounds the heart of one sent far in marriage."

sentences.zh: 上聞而惡之，禮賜益薄。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he was displeased, and the gifts and courtesies bestowed grew ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was displeased, and the gifts and courtesies bestowed upon her grew ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 公主復與西面突厥泥利可汗連結，上恐其爲變，將圖之。

translations.literal: The princess again allied with Nili Qaghan of the Western Turks; the emperor feared she would cause trouble and planned against her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess again allied with Nili Qaghan of the Western Turks. The emperor feared she would cause trouble and began plotting against her.

sentences.zh: 會主與所從胡私通，因發其事，下詔廢黜之。

translations.literal: It happened that the princess had a secret affair with a Hu man who accompanied her; the matter was exposed and an edict deposed her.
translations.idiomatic: When it was discovered that the princess had a secret affair with a Hu attendant, the matter was exposed and an edict deposed her.

sentences.zh: 恐都藍不從，遣奇章公牛弘將美妓四人以啖之。

translations.literal: Fearing Dulü would not comply, he dispatched Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, bearing four beautiful courtesans to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Dulü would refuse, the emperor dispatched Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, bearing four beautiful courtesans to win him over.

sentences.zh: 時沙缽略子曰染幹，號突利可汗，居北方，遣使求婚。

translations.literal: At that time Ishbara's son Rangan, styled Tuli Qaghan, dwelt in the north and sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ishbara's son Rangan, styled Tuli Qaghan, who dwelt in the north, sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上令裴矩謂之曰：「當殺大義主者，方許婚。」

translations.literal: The emperor had Pei Ju tell him: "Only when you kill the Princess Dayi will marriage be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Pei Ju tell him: "Only when you kill Princess Dayi will marriage be permitted."

sentences.zh: 突利以爲然，復譖之，都藍因發怒，遂殺公主于帳。

translations.literal: Tuli thought this correct and again slandered her; Dulü was enraged and killed the princess in her tent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli agreed and slandered her again. Enraged, Dulü killed the princess in her tent.

sentences.zh: 都藍與達頭可汗有隙，數相征伐，上和解之，各引兵而去。

translations.literal: Dulü had a rift with Tardu Qaghan and repeatedly campaigned against each other; the emperor mediated between them, and each withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü had a rift with Tardu Qaghan and repeatedly campaigned against each other. The emperor mediated, and each withdrew their troops.

sentences.zh: 十七年，突利遣使來逆女，上舍之太常，教習六禮，妻以宗女安義公主。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Tuli sent envoys to escort his bride; the emperor lodged her at the Ministry of Ceremonies to be instructed in the six rites, and gave him the imperial clanswoman Princess Anyi in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Tuli sent envoys to escort his bride. The emperor lodged her at the Ministry of Ceremonies to be instructed in the six rites of marriage, and gave him the imperial clanswoman Princess Anyi as his wife.

sentences.zh: 上欲離間北夷，故特厚其禮，遣牛弘、蘇威、斛律孝卿相繼爲使，突厥前後遣使入朝三百七十輩。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to sow discord among the northern barbarians and therefore treated them with especial generosity, dispatching Niu Hong, Su Wei, and Hulu Xiaoqing in succession as envoys; the Turks sent envoys to court three hundred and seventy times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to sow discord among the northern tribes and therefore treated Tuli with especial generosity, dispatching Niu Hong, Su Wei, and Hulu Xiaoqing in succession as envoys. The Turks sent envoys to court three hundred and seventy times in all.

sentences.zh: 突利本居北方，以尚主之故，南徙度斤舊鎮，錫賚優厚。

translations.literal: Tuli had originally dwelt in the north; because of his marriage to the princess, he moved south to the old garrison at Dujin and received generous gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli had originally dwelt in the north. Because of his marriage to the princess, he moved south to the old garrison at Dujin and received generous gifts and rewards.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭怒曰：「我大可汗也，反不如染幹！」

translations.literal: Yudoulu said in anger: "I am the Great Qaghan, yet I am treated worse than Rangan!
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu said in anger: "I am the Great Qaghan, yet I am treated worse than Rangan!"

sentences.zh: 於是朝貢遂絕，數爲邊患。

translations.literal: Thereupon tribute to court ceased, and he repeatedly became a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon tribute to court ceased, and he repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔蜀王秀出靈州道以擊之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, an edict ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to advance by the Lingzhou route to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, an edict ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to advance by the Lingzhou route to attack him.

sentences.zh: 明年，又遣漢王諒爲元帥，左僕射高熲率將軍王詧、上柱國趙仲卿並出朔州道，右僕射楊素率柱國李徹、韓僧壽出靈州，上柱國燕榮出幽州，以擊之。

translations.literal: The following year, Prince Liang of Han was again dispatched as commander-in-chief; Left Vice Director Gao Jiong led General Wang Yan and the supreme pillar Zhao Zhongqing by the Shuozhou route, Right Vice Director Yang Su led the pillars Li Che and Han Shoushou from Lingzhou, and the supreme pillar Yan Rong from Youzhou—all to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Prince Liang of Han was dispatched as commander-in-chief. Left Vice Director Gao Jiong led General Wang Yan and the supreme pillar Zhao Zhongqing by the Shuozhou route; Right Vice Director Yang Su led the pillars Li Che and Han Shoushou from Lingzhou; and the supreme pillar Yan Rong from Youzhou—all to attack the Turks.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭與玷厥舉兵攻染幹，盡殺其兄弟子侄，遂度河，入蔚州。

translations.literal: Yudoulu and Dianjue raised troops to attack Rangan, killing all his brothers, sons, and nephews; they then crossed the river and entered You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu and Dianjue raised troops to attack Rangan, killing all his brothers, sons, and nephews. They then crossed the river and entered You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 染幹夜以五騎與隋使長孫晟歸朝。

translations.literal: Rangan fled by night with five horsemen and the Sui envoy Zhangsun Sheng to submit to court.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan fled by night with five horsemen and the Sui envoy Zhangsun Sheng to submit to the Sui court.

sentences.zh: 上令染幹與雍虞閭使者因頭特勤相辯詰，染幹辭直，上乃厚待之。
