translations.literal: The emperor had Rangan debate face to face with Yudoulu's envoy Yintou Teqin; Rangan's words were straightforward, and the emperor thereupon treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Rangan debate face to face with Yudoulu's envoy Yintou Teqin. Rangan spoke plainly and truthfully, and the emperor thereupon treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭弟都速六棄其妻子，與突利歸朝，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Yudoulu's younger brother Dusuliu abandoned his wife and children and submitted to court with Tuli; the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu's younger brother Dusuliu abandoned his wife and children and submitted to court with Tuli. The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 敕染幹與都速六樗蒲，稍稍輸以寶物，用慰其心。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rangan to play chupu with Dusuliu, gradually losing treasures to him to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Rangan to play chupu with Dusuliu, deliberately losing treasures to him to comfort his heart.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，高煩、楊素擊玷厥，大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, Gao Jiong and Yang Su attacked Dianjue and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, Gao Jiong and Yang Su attacked Dianjue and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 拜染幹爲意利珍豆啟民可汗，華言「意智健」也。

translations.literal: Rangan was appointed Yilizhendou Qimin Qaghan—in Chinese, "wise and vigorous."
translations.idiomatic: Rangan was appointed Yilizhendou Qimin Qaghan—in Chinese, meaning "wise and vigorous."

sentences.zh: 啟民上表謝恩曰：「臣既蒙豎立，復改官名，昔日奸心，今悉除去，奉事至尊，不敢違法。」

translations.literal: Qimin submitted a memorial of gratitude, saying: "Your subject, having been installed and given a new title, has cast off all former treacherous intent; serving the Supreme One, I dare not violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin submitted a memorial of gratitude: "Your subject, having been installed and given a new title, has cast off all former treacherous intent. Serving Your Majesty, I dare not violate the law."

sentences.zh: 上於朔州築大利城以居之。

translations.literal: The emperor built Dali Fort at Shuozhou for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built Dali Fort at Shuozhou for him to dwell in.

sentences.zh: 是時安義主已卒，上以宗女義成公主妻之，部落歸者甚衆。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Anyi had died; the emperor gave him the imperial clanswoman Princess Yicheng in marriage, and many tribes returned to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anyi had by then died. The emperor gave him the imperial clanswoman Princess Yicheng in marriage, and many tribes returned to submit.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭又擊之，上復令入塞。

translations.literal: Yudoulu again attacked him; the emperor again ordered him to enter the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yudoulu attacked him again. The emperor again ordered Qimin to enter the frontier passes for protection.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭侵掠不已，遷于河南，在夏、勝二州之間，發徒掘塹數百里，東西拒河，盡爲啟民畜牧之地。

translations.literal: As Yudoulu's raids continued without cease, Qimin was relocated to Henan, between Xia and Sheng prefectures; corvée laborers dug trenches several hundred li long, bounded east and west by the river, all becoming pastureland for Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: As Yudoulu's raids continued, Qimin was relocated to Henan, between Xia and Sheng prefectures. Corvée laborers dug trenches several hundred li long, bounded east and west by the river, all set aside as pastureland for Qimin.

sentences.zh: 於是遣越國公楊素出靈州，行軍總管韓僧壽出慶州，太平公史萬歲出燕州，大將軍姚辯出河州，以擊都藍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duke Yang Su of Yueguo was dispatched from Lingzhou, the marching commander Han Shoushou from Qingzhou, Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping from Yanzhou, and the great general Yao Bian from Hezhou—all to attack Dulü.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Duke Yang Su of Yueguo from Lingzhou, the marching commander Han Shoushou from Qingzhou, Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping from Yanzhou, and the great general Yao Bian from Hezhou—all to attack Dulü.

sentences.zh: 師未出塞，而都藍爲其麾下所殺，達頭自立爲步迦可汗，其國大亂。

translations.literal: Before the armies had crossed the frontier, Dulü was killed by his own subordinates; Tardu installed himself as Bujia Qaghan, and the realm fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies had crossed the frontier, Dulü was killed by his own subordinates. Tardu installed himself as Bujia Qaghan, and the Turkic realm fell into great disorder.

sentences.zh: 遣太平公史萬歲出朔州以擊之，遇達頭於大斤山，虜不戰而遁，追斬首虜二千餘人。

translations.literal: Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping was dispatched from Shuozhou to attack him; encountering Tardu at Mount Dajin, the barbarians fled without fighting; in pursuit more than two thousand heads of barbarians were cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shi Wansui of Taiping was dispatched from Shuozhou to attack Tardu. Encountering him at Mount Dajin, the Turks fled without fighting. In pursuit more than two thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣出靈州，達頭遁逃而去。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang advanced from Lingzhou; Tardu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang advanced from Lingzhou, and Tardu fled.

sentences.zh: 尋遣其弟子俟利伐從磧東攻啟民。

translations.literal: Soon he sent his younger brother's son Yilibo to attack Qimin from east of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu soon sent his nephew Yilibo to attack Qimin from east of the desert.

sentences.zh: 上又發兵助啟民守要路，俟利伐退走入磧。

translations.literal: The emperor again dispatched troops to help Qimin hold the strategic passes; Yilibo retreated and fled into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again dispatched troops to help Qimin hold the strategic passes. Yilibo retreated and fled into the desert.

sentences.zh: 啟民上表陳謝曰：「大隋聖人莫緣可汗，憐養百姓，如天無不覆也，如地無不載也。

translations.literal: Qimin submitted a memorial of thanks, saying: "The Great Sui Sage Qaghan Moyuan pities and nurtures the people, like Heaven that covers all, like Earth that bears all.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin submitted a memorial of thanks: "The Great Sui Sage Qaghan pities and nurtures the people, like Heaven that covers all, like Earth that bears all.

sentences.zh: 諸姓蒙威恩，赤心歸服，並將部落歸投聖人可汗來也。

translations.literal: All clans have received your awesome grace; with loyal hearts they submit, bringing their tribes to join the Sage Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: All clans have received your awesome grace. With loyal hearts they submit, bringing their tribes to join the Sage Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 或南入長城，或住白道，人民羊馬，遍滿山谷。

translations.literal: Some enter south of the Great Wall, some dwell on the White Road—people, sheep, and horses fill every valley.
translations.idiomatic: Some enter south of the Great Wall, some dwell on the White Road—people, sheep, and horses fill every valley.

sentences.zh: 染幹譬如枯木重起枝葉，枯骨重生皮肉，千萬世長與大隋典羊馬也。」

translations.literal: Rangan is like a withered tree sprouting leaves anew, like dry bones regrowing flesh—I shall forever tend sheep and horses for Great Sui for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Rangan is like a withered tree sprouting leaves anew, like dry bones regrowing flesh—I shall forever tend sheep and horses for Great Sui for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，代州總管韓洪爲虜所敗于恆安，廢爲庶人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, the Daizhou commander Han Hong was defeated by the barbarians at Heng'an and was demoted to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, the Daizhou commander Han Hong was defeated by the Turks at Heng'an and was demoted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 詔楊素爲雲州道行軍元帥，率啟民北征。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yang Su as marching commander-in-chief of the Yunzhou route, leading Qimin on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yang Su as marching commander-in-chief of the Yunzhou route, leading Qimin on a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 斛薛等諸姓初附於啟民，至是而叛。

translations.literal: The Huxie and other clans had initially submitted to Qimin; at this time they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Huxie and other clans had initially submitted to Qimin but now rebelled.

sentences.zh: 素軍河北，值突厥阿勿思力俟斤等南度，掠啟民男女六千口、雜畜二十余萬而去。

translations.literal: Su's army was north of the river when the Turks Abusi Yilibo and others crossed south, plundering six thousand men and women of Qimin's people and more than two hundred thousand mixed livestock before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Su's army was north of the river when the Turks Abusi Yilibo and others crossed south, plundering six thousand of Qimin's people and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock before departing.

sentences.zh: 素率上大將軍梁默輕騎追之，轉戰六十餘里，大破俟斤，悉得人畜以歸啟民。

translations.literal: Su led the supreme general Liang Mo with light cavalry in pursuit; fighting over more than sixty li, he routed Yilibo utterly and returned all the people and livestock to Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: Su led the supreme general Liang Mo with light cavalry in pursuit. After fighting over more than sixty li, he routed Yilibo and returned all the people and livestock to Qimin.

sentences.zh: 素又遣柱國張定和、領軍大將軍劉升別路邀擊，並多斬獲而還。

translations.literal: Su also dispatched the pillars Zhang Dinghe and the commanding general Liu Sheng by separate routes to intercept; both killed and captured many before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Su also dispatched the pillars Zhang Dinghe and the commanding general Liu Sheng by separate routes to intercept. Both killed and captured many before returning.

sentences.zh: 兵既渡河，賊復掠啟民部落，素率驃騎范貴于窟結谷東南奮擊，復破之，追奔八十餘里。

translations.literal: After the troops had crossed the river, the bandits again plundered Qimin's tribe; Su led the swift cavalry commander Fan Gui in a fierce attack southeast of Kujie Valley, again defeating them and pursuing the fleeing enemy over eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops had crossed the river, the raiders again plundered Qimin's tribe. Su led the swift cavalry commander Fan Gui in a fierce attack southeast of Kujie Valley, defeating them again and pursuing the fleeing enemy over eighty li.

sentences.zh: 是歲，泥利可汗及葉護俱被鐵勒所敗。

translations.literal: That year, both Nili Qaghan and Yehu were defeated by the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: That year, both Nili Qaghan and Yehu were defeated by the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 步迦尋亦大亂，奚、霫五部內徙，步迦奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Bujia soon also fell into great disorder; the five Xi and Mohe tribes moved inward, and Bujia fled to the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Bujia soon also fell into great disorder. The five Xi and Mohe tribes moved inward, and Bujia fled to the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 啟民遂有其衆，歲遣朝貢。

translations.literal: Qimin thereupon came to possess their followers and sent tribute to court each year.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin thereupon came to possess their followers and sent tribute to court each year.

sentences.zh: 大業三年四月，煬帝幸榆林，啟民及義成公主來朝行宮，前後獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Daye, Emperor Yang visited Yulin; Qimin and Princess Yicheng came to pay court at the traveling palace, presenting three thousand horses in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Daye, Emperor Yang visited Yulin. Qimin and Princess Yicheng came to pay court at the traveling palace, presenting three thousand horses in all.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物萬二千段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed twelve thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed twelve thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 啟民上表曰：「已前聖人先帝莫緣可汗存在之日，憐臣，賜臣安義公主，種種無少短。

translations.literal: Qimin submitted a memorial, saying: "In former days when the Sage Former Emperor Moyuan Qaghan was alive, he pitied your subject, bestowed Princess Anyi upon me, and in every way showed no shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin submitted a memorial: "In former days when the Sage Former Emperor was alive, he pitied your subject, bestowed Princess Anyi upon me, and in every way showed no shortcoming.

sentences.zh: 臣種末爲聖人先帝憐養，臣兄弟妒惡，相共殺臣，臣當時無處去，向上看只見天，下看只見地，實憶聖人先帝言語，投命去來。

translations.literal: Your subject's clan was pitied and nurtured by the Sage Former Emperor; my brothers envied and hated me and together tried to kill me. At that time I had nowhere to go—looking up I saw only Heaven, looking down I saw only Earth. Truly remembering the Sage Former Emperor's words, I entrusted my life and came.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's clan was pitied and nurtured by the Sage Former Emperor, but my brothers envied and hated me and together tried to kill me. I had nowhere to go—looking up I saw only Heaven, looking down I saw only Earth. Remembering the Sage Former Emperor's words, I entrusted my life to him and came.

sentences.zh: 聖人先帝見臣，大憐臣，死命養活，勝於往前，遣臣作大可汗坐著也。

translations.literal: The Sage Former Emperor saw your subject, greatly pitied me, kept me alive at the cost of his own life, better than before, and installed me as Great Qaghan to sit upon the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Former Emperor saw your subject, greatly pitied me, kept me alive at the cost of his own effort, better than before, and installed me as Great Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 其突厥百姓，死者以外，還聚作百姓也。

translations.literal: Of the Turkic people, aside from the dead, the rest gathered again to become subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Turkic people, aside from the dead, the rest gathered again as his subjects.

sentences.zh: 至尊今還如聖人先帝，捉天下四方坐也。

translations.literal: Your Supreme Majesty now is again like the Sage Former Emperor, holding all within the four directions upon the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Your Supreme Majesty now is again like the Sage Former Emperor, holding all within the four directions upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 還養活臣及突厥百姓，實無少短。

translations.literal: Again nurturing your subject and the Turkic people—truly showing no shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Again nurturing your subject and the Turkic people—truly showing no shortcoming.

sentences.zh: 臣今憶想聖人及至尊養活事，具奏不可盡，並至尊聖心裏在。

translations.literal: Your subject now recalls the nurturing deeds of the Sage and Your Supreme Majesty; though I report them all, they cannot be fully told—all are within Your Supreme Majesty's sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now recalls the nurturing deeds of the Sage and Your Supreme Majesty. Though I report them all, they cannot be fully told—all are within Your Supreme Majesty's sacred heart.

sentences.zh: 臣今非是舊日邊地突厥可汗，臣即是至尊臣民，至尊憐臣時，乞依大國服飾法用，一同華夏。

translations.literal: Your subject is no longer the old frontier Turkic qaghan; I am Your Supreme Majesty's subject and citizen. When Your Supreme Majesty pities your subject, I beg to follow the great state's dress and customs, becoming one with the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is no longer the old frontier Turkic qaghan; I am Your Supreme Majesty's subject and citizen. When Your Supreme Majesty pities your subject, I beg to follow the great state's rules for dress and usage and become one with Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 臣今率部落，敢以上聞，伏願天慈，不違所請。」

translations.literal: Your subject now leads my tribe and dares report this above; humbly I pray for Heaven's compassion, that my request not be denied.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now leads my tribe and dares report this above. Humbly I pray for Heaven's compassion, that my request not be denied."

sentences.zh: 表奏，帝下其議，公卿請依所奏。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor referred it for discussion; the high officials requested compliance with what was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor referred it for discussion. The high officials requested compliance with what was proposed.

sentences.zh: 帝以爲不可，乃下詔曰：「先王建國，夷夏殊風，君子教民，不求變俗。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this unacceptable and issued an edict: "The ancient kings established states; Yi and Xia have different customs. The noble man teaches the people without seeking to change their ways.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered this unacceptable and issued an edict: "The ancient kings established states; barbarian and civilized peoples have different customs. The noble man teaches the people without seeking to change their ways.

sentences.zh: 斷發文身，咸安其性，旃裘卉服，各尚所宜，因而利之，其道弘矣。

translations.literal: Cut hair and tattooed bodies—each rests in their nature; felt coats and grass garments—each honors what suits them. Working with this, the Way is vast indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cut hair and tattooed bodies—each rests in their nature; felt coats and grass garments—each honors what suits them. Working with this, the Way is vast indeed.

sentences.zh: 何必化諸削衽，縻以長纓，豈遂性之至理，非包含之遠度。

translations.literal: Why must all be transformed to cut their lapels and be tethered with long cords? Is this following nature to its utmost principle, or is it not the far-reaching measure of all-embracing tolerance?
translations.idiomatic: Why must all be transformed to cut their lapels and be tethered with long cords? Is this following nature to its utmost principle, or is it not the far-reaching measure of all-embracing tolerance?

sentences.zh: 衣服不同，既辨要荒之敘，庶類區別，彌見天地之情。」

translations.literal: Different clothing already distinguishes the order of the frontier wilderness; distinguishing the myriad kinds more clearly reveals Heaven and Earth's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Different clothing already distinguishes the order of the frontier wilderness. Distinguishing the myriad peoples more clearly reveals Heaven and Earth's intent."

sentences.zh: 仍璽書答啟民，以爲磧北未靜，猶須征戰，但使好心孝順，何必改變衣服也。

translations.literal: He still sent an imperial letter in reply to Qimin, stating that north of the desert was not yet pacified and campaigning was still needed; so long as he kept a good heart and was filial and obedient, why must he change his clothing?
translations.idiomatic: He still sent an imperial letter in reply to Qimin, stating that north of the desert was not yet pacified and campaigning was still needed. So long as he kept a good heart and was filial and obedient, why must he change his clothing?

sentences.zh: 帝法駕御千人大帳，享啟民及其部落酋長三千五百人，賜物二十萬段，其下各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor in imperial procession entered a tent for a thousand men and feasted Qimin and three thousand five hundred chieftains of his tribe, bestowing two hundred thousand bolts of goods, with lesser amounts for those below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in imperial procession entered a tent for a thousand men and feasted Qimin and three thousand five hundred chieftains of his tribe, bestowing two hundred thousand bolts of goods, with lesser amounts for those of lower rank.

sentences.zh: 復下詔曰：「德合天地，覆載所以弗遣，功格區宇，聲教所以鹹洎。

translations.literal: He again issued an edict: "Virtue matches Heaven and Earth; none is excluded from covering and bearing. Merit reaches the realm; none is excluded from sound and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He again issued an edict: "Virtue matches Heaven and Earth; none is excluded from its covering and bearing. Merit reaches the realm; none is excluded from its sound and transformation.

sentences.zh: 至於梯山航海，請受正朔，襲冠解辮，同彼臣民。

translations.literal: As for climbing mountains and crossing seas to request the calendar, adopting caps and unbraiding hair to become subjects like the rest—
translations.idiomatic: Peoples climb mountains and cross seas to request the calendar, adopt caps and unbraid their hair to become subjects like the rest—

sentences.zh: 是故《王會》納貢，義彰前冊，呼韓入臣，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: therefore the 'Royal Assembly' records tribute, righteousness shown in former annals; Huhanye entered as subject and was treated with special ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: as the 'Royal Assembly' records tribute and former annals show righteousness; as Huhanye entered as subject and was treated with special ceremony.

sentences.zh: 突厥意利珍豆啟民可汗志懷沈毅，世修籓職。

translations.literal: The Turkic Yilizhendou Qimin Qaghan's will is deep and resolute; for generations he has maintained frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Yilizhendou Qimin Qaghan's will is deep and resolute; for generations he has maintained his frontier duties.

sentences.zh: 往者挺身違難，拔足歸仁，先朝嘉此款誠，授以徽號。

translations.literal: Formerly he stood forth against adversity and withdrew his feet to return to benevolence; the former court commended this sincere pledge and granted him an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly he stood forth against adversity and withdrew to return to benevolence. The former court commended this sincere pledge and granted him an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 資其甲兵之衆，收其破滅之餘，復祀於既亡之國，繼絕於不存之地。

translations.literal: Supplying him with armed forces, gathering the remnants of destruction, restoring sacrifices in a state already perished, continuing the line in a land no longer existing.
translations.idiomatic: Supplying him with armed forces, gathering the remnants of destruction, restoring sacrifices in a state already perished, continuing the line in a land no longer existing.

sentences.zh: 斯固施均亭育，澤漸要荒者矣。

translations.literal: This is indeed extending equal nurturing, grace reaching the frontier wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed extending equal nurturing, grace reaching even the frontier wilderness.

sentences.zh: 朕以薄德，祗奉靈命，思播遠猷，光融今緒，是以親巡朔野，撫寧籓服。

translations.literal: I, with meager virtue, reverently receive the divine mandate, thinking to spread far-reaching plans and illuminate the present age; therefore I personally tour the northern wilds and pacify the frontier subjects.
translations.idiomatic: I, with meager virtue, reverently receive the divine mandate, thinking to spread far-reaching plans and illuminate the present age. Therefore I personally tour the northern wilds and pacify the frontier subjects.

sentences.zh: 啟民深委誠心，入奉朝覲，率其種落，拜首軒墀，言念丹款，良以嘉尚。

translations.literal: Qimin deeply entrusted his sincere heart, came to pay court, led his tribes, bowed his head at the palace steps; reflecting on his loyal pledge, I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin deeply entrusted his sincere heart, came to pay court, and led his tribes to bow their heads at the palace steps. Reflecting on his loyal pledge, I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 宜隆榮數，式優恆典。

translations.literal: It is fitting to elevate his honors and accord him exceptional standing by permanent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to elevate his honors and accord him exceptional standing by permanent precedent.

sentences.zh: 可賜路車、乘馬、鼓吹、幡旗，贊拜不名，位在諸侯王上。」

translations.literal: He may be granted a state carriage, riding horses, musical ensembles, banners and flags; in announcements of obeisance his name need not be spoken; his rank shall be above all feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: He shall be granted a state carriage, riding horses, musical ensembles, banners and flags. In announcements of obeisance his name need not be spoken, and his rank shall be above all feudal princes."

sentences.zh: 帝親巡雲內，泝金河而東，北幸啟民所居。

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured Yunnei, followed the Jin River eastward, and proceeded north to visit where Qimin dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally toured Yunnei, followed the Jin River eastward, and proceeded north to visit where Qimin dwelt.

sentences.zh: 啟民奉觴上壽，跪伏甚恭。

translations.literal: Qimin raised a cup to offer congratulations on longevity, kneeling and prostrating himself most respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin raised a cup to offer congratulations on the emperor's longevity, kneeling and prostrating himself most respectfully.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賦詩曰：「鹿塞鴻旗駐，龍庭翠輦回。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and composed a poem: "At Deer Pass the great banner halts; from the Dragon Court the emerald carriage returns.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and composed a poem: "At Deer Pass the great banner halts; from the Dragon Court the emerald carriage returns.

sentences.zh: 氈帳望風舉，穹廬向日開。

translations.literal: Felt tents rise at the wind's approach; domed lodges open toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Felt tents rise at the wind's approach; domed lodges open toward the sun.

sentences.zh: 呼韓頓顙至，屠耆接踵來。

translations.literal: Huhanye arrives knocking forehead; the chanyu follow one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Huhanye arrives knocking his forehead; the chanyu follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 索辮擎膻肉，韋韝獻酒杯。

translations.literal: With braided hair they bear mutton; with leather quivers they offer wine cups.
translations.idiomatic: With braided hair they bear mutton; with leather quivers they offer wine cups.

sentences.zh: 何如漢天子，空上單于台。」

translations.literal: How unlike the Han Son of Heaven, who vainly ascended the Chanyu Terrace!
translations.idiomatic: How unlike the Han emperor, who vainly ascended the Chanyu Terrace!"

sentences.zh: 帝賜啟民及主金甕各一，及衣服被褥錦彩，特勤以下各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed upon Qimin and the princess each one golden urn, as well as clothing, bedding, brocades, and silks; Teqin and those below received gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed upon Qimin and the princess each a golden urn, as well as clothing, bedding, brocades, and silks. Teqin and those of lower rank received gifts according to their station.

sentences.zh: 先是，高麗私通使啟民所，啟民推誠奉國，不敢隱境外之交。

translations.literal: Earlier, Goguryeo had sent secret envoys to Qimin's domain; Qimin, with sincere loyalty to the state, dared not conceal foreign contacts beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Goguryeo had sent secret envoys to Qimin's domain. Qimin, with sincere loyalty to the state, dared not conceal foreign contacts beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 是日，將高麗使人見，敕令牛弘宣旨謂之曰：「朕以啟民誠心奉國，故親至其所。

translations.literal: That day the Goguryeo envoys were brought to audience; an edict ordered Niu Hong to proclaim the intent, saying: "I, because Qimin serves the state with sincere heart, have therefore come personally to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Goguryeo envoys were brought to audience. An edict ordered Niu Hong to proclaim: "Because Qimin serves the state with sincere heart, I have come personally to his domain.

sentences.zh: 明年當往涿郡。

translations.literal: Next year I shall go to Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall go to Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 爾還日，語高麗王知，宜早來朝，勿自疑懼。

translations.literal: When you return, tell the King of Goguryeo to know: he should come early to court and not doubt or fear.
translations.idiomatic: When you return, tell the King of Goguryeo: he should come early to court and not doubt or fear.

sentences.zh: 存育之禮， 當同於啟民。

translations.literal: The rites of preservation and nurturing shall be the same as for Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesies of protection and support shall be the same as those accorded Qimin.

sentences.zh: 如或不朝，必將啟民巡行彼土。」

translations.literal: If he does not come to court, I shall certainly send Qimin to patrol his lands.
translations.idiomatic: If he fails to come to court, I shall certainly have Qimin patrol his territory."

sentences.zh: 使人甚懼。

translations.literal: This made the envoys greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: This left the envoys deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 啟民仍扈從入塞，至定襄，詔令歸籓。

translations.literal: Qimin again followed in attendance into the frontier passes; reaching Dingxiang, an edict ordered him to return to vassal status.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin again followed the emperor into the frontier and, upon reaching Dingxiang, was ordered by edict to resume his vassal duties.

sentences.zh: 明年，朝於東都，禮賜益厚。

translations.literal: The next year he came to court at the Eastern Capital, and the rites and gifts grew ever more generous.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court at the Eastern Capital, where the honors and gifts bestowed upon him grew ever more lavish.

sentences.zh: 是歲，疾終，上爲之廢朝三日，立其子咄吉世，是爲始畢可汗。

translations.literal: That year he died of illness; the emperor suspended court for three days on his account and installed his son Tudiji, who became Shibi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died of illness. The emperor suspended court for three days in mourning and installed his son Tudiji as Shibi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 表請尚公主，詔從其俗。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting marriage to an imperial princess; an edict granted this according to their custom.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting marriage to an imperial princess, and an edict granted the request according to Turkic custom.

sentences.zh: 十一年，來朝於東都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he came to court at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 其年，車駕避暑汾陽宮，八月，始畢率其種落入寇，圍帝於雁門。

translations.literal: That year, as the imperial carriage summered at Fenyang Palace, in the eighth month Shibi led his tribes in raiding and besieged the emperor at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while the emperor was summering at Fenyang Palace, Shibi led his tribes in a raid in the eighth month and besieged the emperor at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 詔諸郡發兵赴行在所，援軍方至，始畢引去。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the commanderies to dispatch troops to the emperor's location; relief forces had just arrived when Shibi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the commanderies to dispatch troops to the emperor's location. Relief forces had barely arrived when Shibi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由是朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: From this the tribute missions ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, tribute missions ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 明年，復寇馬邑，唐公以兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The next year he raided Mayi again; the Duke of Tang drove him off with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he raided Mayi again, but the Duke of Tang drove him off with troops.

sentences.zh: 隋末亂離，中國人歸之者無數，遂大強盛，勢陵中夏。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, amid turmoil and separation, countless Chinese submitted to him; he thus grew greatly powerful, his might overshadowing the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, amid chaos and upheaval, countless Chinese submitted to him. He grew immensely powerful, and his might came to overshadow the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 迎蕭皇后，置於定襄。

translations.literal: He welcomed Empress Xiao and installed her at Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Empress Xiao and established her at Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 薛舉、竇建德、王世充、劉武周、梁師都、李軌、高開道之徒，雖僭尊號，皆北面稱臣，受其可汗之號。

translations.literal: Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, Gao Kaidao, and the like, though they usurped exalted titles, all turned north to declare themselves subjects and received qaghan titles from him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, Gao Kaidao, and others, though they had usurped royal titles, all turned north to declare themselves his subjects and accepted qaghan titles from him.

sentences.zh: 使者往來，相望於道也。

translations.literal: Envoys traveled back and forth, visible to one another along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys traveled back and forth in such numbers that they could be seen all along the roads.

sentences.zh: 西突厥

translations.literal: Western Turks
translations.idiomatic: Western Turks

sentences.zh: 西突厥者，木杆可汗之子大邏便也。

translations.literal: The Western Turks were Daluobian, son of Mughan Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks were descended from Daluobian, son of Mughan Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 與沙鉢略有隙，因分為二，漸以強盛。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Ishbara and therefore split into two; gradually he grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: After a falling-out with Ishbara, the Turks split into two realms, and the Western branch gradually grew powerful.

sentences.zh: 東拒都斤，西越金山，龜茲、鐵勒、伊吾及西域諸胡悉附之。

translations.literal: To the east he held at Dujin; to the west he crossed Jinshan. Kucha, the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the Hu peoples of the Western Regions submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: To the east he held the line at Dujin; to the west he crossed the Altai Mountains. Kucha, the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the Hu peoples of the Western Regions submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 大邏便爲處羅侯所執，其國立鞅素特勤之子，是爲泥利可汗。

translations.literal: Daluobian was seized by Chuluohou; the realm installed the son of Yangsu Teqin, who became Nili Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian was seized by Chuluohou, and the realm installed the son of Yangsu Teqin as Nili Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 卒，子達漫立，號泥撅處羅可汗。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Daman was installed, styled Nijue Chuluo Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death, his son Daman was installed and styled Nijue Chuluo Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 其母向氏，本中國人，生達漫而泥利卒，向氏又嫁其弟婆實特勤。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Xiang, was originally a Chinese; she bore Daman, and after Nili died Lady Xiang married his younger brother Poshi Teqin.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xiang, was originally Chinese. She bore Daman, and after Nili's death she married his younger brother Poshi Teqin.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，婆實共向氏入朝，遇達頭亂，遂留京師，每舍之鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, Poshi entered court together with Lady Xiang; encountering Datou's rebellion, they remained in the capital and were lodged at the Honglu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaihuang era, Poshi entered court together with Lady Xiang. With Datou's rebellion underway, they remained in the capital and were lodged at the Honglu Temple.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗居無恆處，然多在烏孫故地。

translations.literal: Chuluo Qaghan had no fixed residence, yet he mostly dwelt in the former lands of Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo Qaghan had no fixed residence, though he spent most of his time in the former territory of Wusun.

sentences.zh: 復立二小可汗，分統所部。

translations.literal: He further installed two lesser qaghans to command his divisions separately.
translations.idiomatic: He further installed two lesser qaghans to govern his divisions separately.

sentences.zh: 一在石國北，以制諸胡國。

translations.literal: One was north of Shiguo, to control the various Hu states.
translations.idiomatic: One was stationed north of Shiguo to control the various Hu states.

sentences.zh: 一居龜茲北，其地名應娑。

translations.literal: One dwelt north of Kucha, at a place called Yingsa.
translations.idiomatic: The other dwelt north of Kucha, at a place called Yingsa.

sentences.zh: 官有俟發、閻洪達，以評議國事，自余與東國同。

translations.literal: Among officials were Yifa and Yan Hongda, who deliberated on state affairs; the rest was the same as in the Eastern realm.
translations.idiomatic: Among his officials were Yifa and Yan Hongda, who deliberated on state affairs. The rest of the government was organized like that of the Eastern Turks.

sentences.zh: 每五月八日，相聚祭神，歲遣重臣向其先世所居之窟致祭焉。

translations.literal: Every eighth day of the fifth month they gathered to sacrifice to the spirits; each year they sent high ministers to offer sacrifice at the cave where their forebears had dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Every year on the eighth day of the fifth month they gathered to sacrifice to the spirits, and each year they dispatched high ministers to offer sacrifice at the cave where their forebears had once lived.

sentences.zh: 當大業初，處羅可汗撫御無道，其國多叛，與鐵勒屢相攻，大爲鐵勒所敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era, Chuluo Qaghan governed without proper rule; many in his realm rebelled, and he repeatedly fought the Tiele and was greatly defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era, Chuluo Qaghan governed harshly and unjustly. Many of his subjects rebelled, and after repeated clashes with the Tiele he suffered major defeats.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎裴矩在敦煌引致西域，聞國亂，復知處羅思其母氏，因奏之。

translations.literal: At that time Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Ju was in Dunhuang attracting the Western Regions; hearing of turmoil in the realm and also knowing that Chuluo missed his mother, he memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Ju was in Dunhuang working to draw the Western Regions into contact with Sui. Learning of the turmoil in Chuluo's realm and knowing that Chuluo missed his mother, he memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣司朝謁者崔君肅齎書慰諭之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Palace Usher Cui Junsu bearing a letter to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched Palace Usher Cui Junsu with a letter of comfort and instruction.

sentences.zh: 處羅甚踞，受詔不肯起。

translations.literal: Chuluo was very haughty; receiving the edict he refused to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo was extremely arrogant and refused to rise when he received the edict.

sentences.zh: 君肅謂處羅曰：「突厥本一國也，中分爲二，自相仇敵。

translations.literal: Junsu said to Chuluo: "The Turks were originally one realm; they split in two and became mutual enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said to Chuluo: "The Turks were originally one people, but they split in two and became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 每歲交兵，積數十年而莫能相滅者，明知啟民與處羅國其勢敵耳。

translations.literal: Each year they exchanged arms; for decades accumulated neither could destroy the other — clearly because Qimin's realm and Chuluo's realm are evenly matched in strength.
translations.idiomatic: They have fought year after year for decades without either side destroying the other, which shows plainly that Qimin's realm and yours are evenly matched in strength.

sentences.zh: 今啟民舉其部落，兵且百萬，入臣天子，甚有丹誠者，何也？

translations.literal: Now Qimin has moved his entire tribe, with nearly a million troops, to submit as subject to the Son of Heaven — with very sincere loyalty indeed. Why is that?
translations.idiomatic: Now Qimin has brought his entire tribe — nearly a million warriors — to submit to the Son of Heaven with such evident sincerity. Why do you think that is?

sentences.zh: 但以切恨可汗而不能獨制，故卑事天子以借漢兵，連二大國，欲滅可汗耳。

translations.literal: It is only because he deeply hates the Qaghan yet cannot subdue him alone, and therefore humbles himself before the Son of Heaven to borrow Han troops, joining two great realms to destroy the Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Because he deeply resents you yet cannot overcome you alone, he has humbled himself before the Son of Heaven to borrow Han troops, intending to join two great powers and destroy you.

sentences.zh: 百官兆庶咸請許之，天子弗違，師出有日矣。

translations.literal: All officials and the myriad people alike petitioned that it be granted; the Son of Heaven did not refuse, and the day of marching forth draws near.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike petitioned for approval, and the Son of Heaven did not refuse. The day of marching forth draws near.

sentences.zh: 顧可汗母向氏，本中國人，歸在京師，處於賓館。

translations.literal: But the Qaghan's mother, Lady Xiang, is originally Chinese; she has returned to the capital and is lodged in the guest residence.
translations.idiomatic: But your mother, Lady Xiang, is originally Chinese. She now lives in the capital, lodged in the guest residence.

sentences.zh: 聞天子之詔，懼可汗之滅，旦夕守闕，哭泣悲哀。

translations.literal: Hearing the Son of Heaven's edict, she feared the Qaghan's destruction; day and night she kept vigil at the palace gate, weeping in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard the Son of Heaven's edict, she feared for your destruction. Day and night she kept vigil at the palace gate, weeping in grief.

sentences.zh: 是以天子憐焉，爲其輟策。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven took pity on her and halted the campaign on her account.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven took pity on her and halted the campaign on her account.

sentences.zh: 向夫人又匍匐謝罪，因請發使以召可汗，令入內屬，乞加恩禮，同於啟民。

translations.literal: Lady Xiang again prostrated herself to beg forgiveness and requested that envoys be sent to summon the Qaghan, that he enter inner submission, and that favor and rites be added equal to Qimin's.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiang prostrated herself again to beg forgiveness and asked that envoys be sent to summon you, that you submit as an inner vassal, and that you receive the same honors as Qimin.

sentences.zh: 天子從之，故遣使到此。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven consented, and therefore dispatched envoys to this place.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven agreed, and that is why envoys have been sent here.

sentences.zh: 可汗若稱籓拜詔，國乃永安，而母得延壽；

translations.literal: If the Qaghan declares himself vassal and bows to receive the edict, the realm will then be forever secure and his mother will gain extended life;
translations.idiomatic: If you declare yourself a vassal and bow to receive the edict, your realm will be secure and your mother will be spared;

sentences.zh: 不然者，則向夫人爲誑天子，必當取戮而傳首虜庭。

translations.literal: if not, then Lady Xiang will have deceived the Son of Heaven and will certainly be executed, her head sent to the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise Lady Xiang will be judged to have deceived the Son of Heaven, and she will certainly be executed with her head sent to your court.

sentences.zh: 發大隋之兵，資北蕃之衆，左提右挈，以擊可汗，死亡則無日矣。

translations.literal: Mobilizing Great Sui's troops and supplying the northern tribes' multitudes, taking you in left hand and right, they will strike the Qaghan — the day of death will not be far off.
translations.idiomatic: Great Sui will mobilize its armies and supply the northern tribes, and with forces closing in from every side, your day of death will not be far off.

sentences.zh: 奈何惜兩拜之禮，剿慈母之命，吝一句稱臣，喪匈奴國也！」

translations.literal: How can you begrudge two bows of ritual, cut short your loving mother's life, stint on a single phrase of subjecthood, and lose the Xiongnu realm!
translations.idiomatic: How can you begrudge two bows of submission, cut short your loving mother's life, refuse a single phrase declaring yourself subject, and lose your realm!"

sentences.zh: 處羅聞之，矍然而起，流涕再拜，跪受詔書。

translations.literal: When Chuluo heard this, he started up in alarm, wept as he bowed twice, and knelt to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuluo heard this, he started up in alarm, wept as he bowed twice, and knelt to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 君肅又說處羅曰：「啟民內附，先帝嘉之，賞賜極厚，故致兵強國富。

translations.literal: Junsu further persuaded Chuluo, saying: "When Qimin submitted inwardly, the former emperor praised him and bestowed extremely generous gifts, thus making his troops strong and his realm rich.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu went on to persuade Chuluo: "When Qimin submitted to the court, the former emperor praised him and bestowed extremely generous gifts, which made his forces strong and his realm prosperous.

sentences.zh: 今可汗後附，與之爭寵，須深結于天子，自表至誠。

translations.literal: Now the Qaghan submits later and contends with him for favor; you must deeply bind yourself to the Son of Heaven and display utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you submit later and must compete with him for favor, you must forge a deep bond with the Son of Heaven and show the utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 既以道遠，未得朝覲，宜立一功，以明臣節。」

translations.literal: Since the road is far and you have not yet been able to attend court, you should establish one achievement to make clear your subject's devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Since the distance is great and you have not yet been able to attend court, you should perform some service to demonstrate your loyalty as a subject."

sentences.zh: 處羅曰：「如何？」

translations.literal: Chuluo said: "How?"
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo asked: "How?"

sentences.zh: 君肅曰：「吐谷渾者，啟民少子莫賀咄設之母家也。

translations.literal: Junsu said: "The Tuyuhun are the maternal kin of Mohezhuo She, Qimin's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said: "The Tuyuhun are the maternal kin of Mohezhuo She, Qimin's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 今天子又以義成公主妻于啟民，啟民畏天子之威而與之絕。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven has also given Princess Yicheng in marriage to Qimin; Qimin, fearing the Son of Heaven's authority, has broken with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has also given Princess Yicheng in marriage to Qimin, and Qimin, fearing the emperor's authority, has broken with them.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾亦因憾漢故，職貢不修。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun also, because of resentment toward Han, have neglected tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun, resentful toward the Han court, have also neglected their tribute duties.

sentences.zh: 可汗若請誅之，天子必許。

translations.literal: If the Qaghan requests their destruction, the Son of Heaven will certainly grant it.
translations.idiomatic: If you request permission to destroy them, the Son of Heaven will certainly grant it.

sentences.zh: 漢擊其內，可汗攻其外，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Han strikes from within, the Qaghan attacks from without — their defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Han will strike from within while you attack from without, and their defeat is certain.

sentences.zh: 然後身自入朝，道路無阻，因見老母，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Then you may personally enter court; the roads will be unobstructed, and you may thereby see your old mother — is that not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Then you may come to court in person, the roads will be open, and you may see your aged mother—would that not be fitting?"

sentences.zh: 處羅大喜，遂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Chuluo was greatly pleased and therefore dispatched envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo was greatly pleased and dispatched envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝將西狩，六年，遣侍御史韋節召處羅，令與車駕會於大鬥拔穀。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to hunt westward; in the sixth year he dispatched Attendant Censor Wei Jie to summon Chuluo, ordering him to meet the imperial carriage at Dabagu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to hunt in the west, in the sixth year he dispatched Attendant Censor Wei Jie to summon Chuluo and ordered him to meet the imperial procession at Dabagu.

sentences.zh: 其國人不從，處羅謝使者，辭以他故。

translations.literal: The people of his realm would not follow; Chuluo apologized to the envoy and declined on other grounds.
translations.idiomatic: His people refused to go, and Chuluo apologized to the envoy, declining on other grounds.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered but could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious but could do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 適會其酋長射匱遣使來求婚，裴矩因奏曰：「處羅不朝，恃強大耳。

translations.literal: It happened that the chieftain Shegui sent envoys seeking marriage; Pei Ju therefore memorialized, saying: "Chuluo does not come to court — he relies merely on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the chieftain Shegui sent envoys seeking marriage. Pei Ju memorialized: "Chuluo refuses to come to court because he relies on his strength alone.

sentences.zh: 臣請以計弱之，分裂其國，即易制也。

translations.literal: Your servant requests to weaken him by stratagem, split his realm, and then he will be easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to weaken him by stratagem, split his realm, and then he will be easy to control.

sentences.zh: 射匱者，都六之子，達頭之孫，世爲可汗，君臨西面。

translations.literal: Shegui is the son of Duliu and grandson of Datou; for generations his line has been qaghan, ruling the western domains.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui is the son of Duliu and grandson of Datou. His line has held the qaghanate for generations and rules the western domains.

sentences.zh: 今聞其失職，附隸于處羅，故遣使來，以結援耳。

translations.literal: Now hearing that he has lost his office and attached himself subordinately to Chuluo, he therefore sent envoys to forge an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he had lost his position and submitted to Chuluo, he sent envoys to seek an alliance.

sentences.zh: 願厚禮其使，拜爲大可汗，則突厥勢分，兩從我矣。」

translations.literal: I wish to treat his envoys generously and invest him as Great Qaghan; then Turkic power will be divided, and both will follow us.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty treats his envoys generously and invests him as Great Qaghan, Turkic power will be divided and both factions will follow us."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 因遣裴矩朝夕至館，微諷諭之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Pei Ju morning and evening to the guest lodge to subtly instruct and persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Pei Ju to the guest lodge morning and evening to subtly persuade them.

sentences.zh: 帝於仁風殿召其使者，言處羅不順之意，稱射匱有好心，吾將立爲大可汗，令發兵誅處羅，然後當爲婚也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned their envoys at Rensfeng Hall, spoke of Chuluo's disobedience, praised Shegui's good intentions, and said he would install him as Great Qaghan, order him to dispatch troops to execute Chuluo, and then the marriage would be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At Rensfeng Hall the emperor summoned Shegui's envoys, spoke of Chuluo's disobedience, praised Shegui's good intentions, and said he would install him as Great Qaghan, have him dispatch troops to destroy Chuluo, and then grant the marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝取桃竹白羽箭一枝以賜射匱，因謂之曰：「此事宜速，使疾如箭也。」

translations.literal: The emperor took one white-feathered arrow of peach bamboo and bestowed it on Shegui, saying to him: "This matter should be swift — make haste like an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took a white-feathered arrow of peach bamboo and bestowed it on Shegui, saying: "Act swiftly in this matter—move as fast as an arrow."

sentences.zh: 使者返，路經處羅，處羅愛箭，將留之，使者譎而得免。

translations.literal: The envoys returned; passing through Chuluo's territory, Chuluo coveted the arrow and was about to keep it, but the envoys deceived him and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys returned. Passing through Chuluo's territory, Chuluo coveted the arrow and tried to keep it, but the envoys tricked him and got away.

sentences.zh: 射匱聞而大喜，興兵襲處羅，處羅大敗，棄妻子，將左右數千騎東走。

translations.literal: Shegui heard and was greatly pleased; he raised troops and attacked Chuluo. Chuluo was utterly defeated, abandoned wife and children, and fled east with several thousand mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui was delighted when he heard the news. He raised troops and attacked Chuluo, who suffered a crushing defeat, abandoned his wife and children, and fled east with several thousand mounted followers.

sentences.zh: 在路又被劫掠，遁于高昌東，保時羅漫山。

translations.literal: On the road he was robbed again; he fled east of Gaochang and took refuge on Mount Shiluo.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he was robbed again. He fled east of Gaochang and took refuge on Mount Shiluo.

sentences.zh: 高昌王麹伯雅上狀，帝遣裴矩將向氏親要左右，馳至玉門關晉昌城。

translations.literal: King Qu Boya of Gaochang submitted a report; the emperor dispatched Pei Ju leading Lady Xiang's close attendants, galloping to Jinchang city at Yumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Boya of Gaochang submitted a report, and the emperor dispatched Pei Ju with Lady Xiang's close attendants, who galloped to Jinchang at Yumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 矩遣向氏使詣處羅所，論朝廷弘養之義，丁寧曉諭之，遂入朝，然每有怏怏之色。

translations.literal: Ju sent Lady Xiang's envoy to Chuluo's location to expound the court's broad policy of nurturing, repeatedly instructing and enlightening him; he then entered court, yet often wore a discontented expression.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju sent an envoy from Lady Xiang to Chuluo's camp to explain the court's generous policy of support and repeatedly urged him to submit. Chuluo then came to court, though he often wore a discontented expression.

sentences.zh: 以七年冬，處羅朝于臨朔宮，帝享之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, Chuluo came to court at Linshuo Palace and the emperor feasted him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year, Chuluo came to court at Linshuo Palace, where the emperor feasted him.

sentences.zh: 處羅稽首謝曰：「臣總西面諸蕃，不得早來朝拜，今參見遲晚，罪責極深，臣心裏悚懼，不能道盡。」

translations.literal: Chuluo kowtowed and apologized, saying: "Your subject governs all the western tribes and could not come early to court; now this audience comes late, and the guilt and blame are extremely deep. In my heart I am fearful and trembling and cannot express it fully.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo kowtowed and apologized: "Your subject governs all the western tribes and could not come to court sooner. This audience comes late, and my guilt is profound. My heart trembles with fear, and words fail me."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「往者與突厥相侵擾，不得安居。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In former times we and the Turks mutually raided and harassed each other and could not live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In former times Turks and Chinese raided and harassed each other, and neither side could live in peace.

sentences.zh: 今四海既清，與一家無異，朕皆欲存養，使遂性靈。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are already clear, no different from one household; I all wish to preserve and nurture, allowing each to follow its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and we are as one family. I wish to preserve and nurture all peoples and let each live according to its nature.

sentences.zh: 譬如天上止有一個日照臨，莫不寧帖；

translations.literal: It is like heaven having only one sun shining down — none are not tranquil and at ease;
translations.idiomatic: It is like heaven having only one sun shining down, under which all live in peace;

sentences.zh: 若有兩個三個日，萬物何以得安？

translations.literal: if there were two or three suns, how could the myriad things find peace?
translations.idiomatic: if there were two or three suns, how could the myriad things find peace?

sentences.zh: 比者亦知處羅總攝事繁，不得早來相見。

translations.literal: Recently I also knew that Chuluo, overseeing many affairs, could not come early to meet.
translations.idiomatic: I also know that you, Chuluo, have had many affairs to oversee and could not come sooner.

sentences.zh: 今日見處羅，懷抱豁然歡喜，處羅亦當豁然，不煩在意。」

translations.literal: Today, seeing Chuluo, my heart is suddenly joyful; Chuluo too should be suddenly at ease and need not trouble himself over it.
translations.idiomatic: Today, seeing you, my heart is filled with joy. You too should put your worries aside and not trouble yourself over this."

sentences.zh: 明年元會，處羅上壽曰：「自天以下，地以上，日月所照，唯有聖人可汗。

translations.literal: The next year at the New Year's assembly, Chuluo offered longevity wishes, saying: "From below heaven to above earth, wherever sun and moon shine, there is only the Sage Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's assembly the following year, Chuluo offered a toast for long life: "From heaven above to earth below, wherever sun and moon shine, there is only the Sage Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 今是大日，願聖人可汗千歲萬歲常如今日也。」

translations.literal: Today is the Great Sun; may the Sage Qaghan live a thousand years, ten thousand years, always as today.
translations.idiomatic: Today you are the Great Sun. May the Sage Qaghan live a thousand years, ten thousand years, always as today."

sentences.zh: 詔留其累弱萬餘口，令其弟達度關牧畜會寧郡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that more than ten thousand of his dependents and the weak be retained, and his younger brother Dadu be sent through the passes to herd livestock in Huining Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that more than ten thousand of his dependents and the weak be retained, and his younger brother Dadu be sent through the passes to herd livestock in Huining Commandery.

sentences.zh: 處羅從征高麗，賜號爲曷薩那可汗，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Chuluo followed the campaign against Goguryeo and was granted the title Hesana Qaghan, with very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo joined the campaign against Goguryeo and was granted the title Hesana Qaghan, with very generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，以信義公主嫁焉，賜錦彩袍千具，彩萬匹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Princess Xinyi was given to him in marriage, with a gift of one thousand brocade robes and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, Princess Xinyi was given to him in marriage, along with one thousand brocade robes and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 帝將復其故地，以遼東之役，故未遑也。

translations.literal: The emperor intended to restore his former lands, but because of the Liaodong campaign, he had not yet had the leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to restore his former lands, but the Liaodong campaign left him no time to do so.

sentences.zh: 每從巡幸。

translations.literal: He always followed on imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: He always accompanied the emperor on imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，隨化及至河北。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he followed Huaji as far as Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Jiangdu he followed Huaji as far as Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及將敗，奔歸京師，爲北蕃突厥所害。

translations.literal: When Huaji was about to be defeated, he fled back to the capital and was killed by the northern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was on the verge of defeat, he fled back to the capital and was killed by the northern Turks.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒之先，匈奴之苗裔也，種類最多。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Tiele were descendants of the Xiongnu; their tribes are the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele traced their origins to the Xiongnu and comprised the greatest number of tribal groups.

sentences.zh: 自西海之東，依據山谷，往往不絕。

translations.literal: From east of the Western Sea, dwelling along valleys and mountains, they appear everywhere without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: From east of the Western Sea they spread along valleys and mountains in an unbroken succession of settlements.

sentences.zh: 獨洛河北有僕骨、同羅、韋紇、拔也古、覆羅並號俟斤，蒙陳、吐如紇、斯結、渾、斛薛等諸姓，勝兵可二萬。

translations.literal: North of the Duluo River were Pugu, Tongluo, Weihe, Bayegu, and Fuluo, all styled irkin, together with the clans Mengchen, Turuhe, Sijie, Hun, and Huxie — able warriors numbering about twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Duluo River lived the Pugu, Tongluo, Weihe, Bayegu, and Fuluo, all styled irkin, along with the Mengchen, Turuhe, Sijie, Hun, and Huxie clans — about twenty thousand warriors in all.

sentences.zh: 伊吾以西，焉耆之北，傍白山，則有契弊、薄落職、乙咥、蘇婆、那曷、烏讙、紇骨、也咥、於尼讙等，勝兵可二萬。

translations.literal: West of Yiwu and north of Yanqi, along White Mountain, were Qibi, Boluozhi, Yidi, Supo, Nahe, Wuyan, Hegu, Yedi, and Yuniyannuan, with able warriors numbering about twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yiwu and north of Yanqi, along White Mountain, lived the Qibi, Boluozhi, Yidi, Supo, Nahe, Wuyan, Hegu, Yedi, and Yuniyannuan tribes — about twenty thousand warriors in all.

sentences.zh: 金山西南，有薛延陀、咥勒兒、十槃、達契等，一萬餘兵。

translations.literal: Southwest of Jinshan were Xueyantuo, Dile'er, Shipan, Daqi, and others, with more than ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the Altai Mountains lived the Xueyantuo, Dile'er, Shipan, Daqi, and others — more than ten thousand warriors in all.

sentences.zh: 康國北，傍阿得水，則有訶咥、曷昚、撥忽、比干、具海、曷比悉、何嵯蘇、拔也未渴達等，有三萬許兵。

translations.literal: North of Kangguo, along the Aideshui River, were Hedi, Heshen, Bohu, Bigan, Juhai, Hebixi, Hesuo, and Bayeweikeda, with about thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: North of Kang and along the Aideshui River lived the Hedi, Heshen, Bohu, Bigan, Juhai, Hebixi, Hesuo, and Bayeweikeda tribes — about thirty thousand warriors in all.

sentences.zh: 得嶷海東西，有蘇路羯、三索咽、蔑促、隆忽等諸姓，八千餘。

translations.literal: East and west of the De'er Sea were the clans Sulujie, Sansuoyan, Miecui, Longhu, and others, numbering more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: East and west of the De'er Sea lived the Sulujie, Sansuoyan, Miecui, Longhu, and other clans — more than eight thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: 拂菻東則有恩屈、阿蘭、北褥九離、伏嗢昏等，近二萬人。

translations.literal: East of Byzantium were Enqu, Alan, Beiru Jiuli, Fu'ohun, and others, nearly twenty thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: East of Byzantium lived the Enqu, Alan, Beiru Jiuli, Fu'ohun, and others — nearly twenty thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: 北海南則都波等。

translations.literal: South of the Northern Sea were Dubo and others.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Northern Sea were the Dubo and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 雖姓氏各別，總謂爲鐵勒。

translations.literal: Although their surnames and clans differed, they were collectively called the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Though their clans bore different names, they were collectively known as the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 並無君長，分屬東、西兩突厥。

translations.literal: None had chieftains or rulers; they were divided among the Eastern and Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: None had chieftains of their own; they were distributed among the Eastern and Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 居無恆所，隨水草流移。

translations.literal: They had no fixed dwellings but moved according to grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: They had no permanent settlements and wandered wherever grass and water led them.

sentences.zh: 人性凶忍，善於騎射，貪婪尤甚，以寇抄爲生。

translations.literal: By nature the people were cruel and fierce, skilled in mounted archery, exceedingly greedy, and made their living by raiding and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: By nature they were cruel and fierce, expert horsemen and archers, and exceedingly greedy — they lived by raiding and plunder.

sentences.zh: 近西邊者，頗爲藝植，多牛羊而少馬。

translations.literal: Those near the western frontier practiced cultivation to some degree; they had many cattle and sheep but few horses.
translations.idiomatic: Those near the western frontier practiced some agriculture; they kept many cattle and sheep but few horses.

sentences.zh: 自突厥有國，東西征討，皆資其用，以制北荒。

translations.literal: From the time the Turks had a state, both their eastern and western campaigns relied on the Tiele for support in controlling the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turks had established their realm, every campaign east and west drew on the Tiele to help subdue the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，晉王廣北征，納啟民，大破步迦可汗，鐵勒於是分散。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, Prince Guang of Jin campaigned north, received Qimin, and greatly defeated Bujia Qaghan; the Tiele consequently scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era, Prince Guang of Jin campaigned north, received Qimin, and routed Bujia Qaghan; the Tiele consequently scattered.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，突厥處羅可汗擊鐵勒諸部，厚稅歛其物，又猜忌薛延陀等，恐為變，遂集其魁帥數百人，盡誅之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye, the Turk Chuluo Qaghan attacked the various Tiele tribes, heavily taxed and seized their goods, and also suspected the Xueyantuo and others; fearing they would rebel, he gathered several hundred of their chiefs and leaders and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye, the Turk Chuluo Qaghan attacked the various Tiele tribes, heavily taxed and seized their goods, and grew suspicious of the Xueyantuo and others. Fearing they would rebel, he gathered several hundred of their chiefs and leaders and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 由是一時反叛，拒處羅，遂立俟利發俟斤契弊歌楞為易勿真莫何可汗，居貪汗山。

translations.literal: Because of this, they all rebelled at once and resisted Chuluo, then established the irkin Qibi Geleng, whose title was Silifa, as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, residing at Tanhan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, they all rebelled at once and resisted Chuluo. They then established the irkin Qibi Geleng, whose title was Silifa, as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, residing at Tanhan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 復立薛延陀內俟斤，字也咥，為小可汗。

translations.literal: They also established the Xueyantuo inner irkin, styled Yezhi, as lesser qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: They also established the Xueyantuo inner irkin, styled Yezhi, as lesser qaghan.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗既敗，莫何可汗始大。

translations.literal: After Chuluo Qaghan was defeated, Mohe Qaghan first became powerful.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuluo Qaghan was defeated, Mohe Qaghan began to grow powerful.

sentences.zh: 莫何勇毅絕倫，甚得眾心，為鄰國所憚，伊吾、高昌、焉耆諸國悉附之。

translations.literal: Mohe was brave and resolute beyond compare, greatly won the hearts of the people, and was feared by neighboring states; Yiwu, Gaochang, Yanqi, and the other states all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe was brave and resolute beyond compare, greatly won the people's loyalty, and was feared by neighboring states; Yiwu, Gaochang, Yanqi, and the other states all attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 其俗大抵與突厥同，唯丈夫婚畢，便就妻家，待產乳男女，然後歸舍，死者埋殯之，此其異也。

translations.literal: Their customs were largely the same as the Turks', except that after a man completed marriage he went at once to his wife's family, and only after she had borne children did he return home; the dead were buried — these were the differences.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were much like those of the Turks, except that after marriage a man went to live with his wife's family and returned home only once she had borne children, and the dead were buried — these were the differences.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，遣使貢方物，自是不絕云。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye they sent envoys to present local products, and from then on tribute was never interrupted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye they sent envoys bearing local products as tribute, and from that time tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 奚本曰庫莫奚，東部胡之種也。

translations.literal: The Xi were originally called the Kumo Xi, a branch of the Eastern Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were originally known as the Kumo Xi, a branch of the Eastern Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 爲慕容氏所破，遺落者竄匿松、漠之間。

translations.literal: They were shattered by the Murong clan; those who survived scattered and hid among the pines and deserts.
translations.idiomatic: The Murong clan shattered them, and those who survived fled into hiding among the pine forests and desert wastes.

sentences.zh: 其俗甚爲不潔，而善射獵，好爲寇鈔。

translations.literal: Their customs were very unclean; they were skilled at shooting and hunting and fond of raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Their ways were notably unclean; they were skilled hunters and archers and fond of raiding.

sentences.zh: 初臣於突厥，後稍強盛，分爲五部：一曰辱紇王，二曰莫賀弗，三曰契個，四曰木昆，五曰室得。

translations.literal: At first they submitted to the Turks; later they gradually grew stronger and divided into five divisions: first, Ruohewang; second, Mohefu; third, Qige; fourth, Mukun; fifth, Shide.
translations.idiomatic: At first they submitted to the Turks, but later they gradually grew stronger and split into five divisions: Ruohewang, Mohefu, Qige, Mukun, and Shide.

sentences.zh: 每部俟斤一人爲其帥。

translations.literal: Each division had one irkin as its commander.
translations.idiomatic: Each division was led by a single irkin as its commander.

sentences.zh: 隨逐水草，頗同突厥。

translations.literal: They followed grass and water, much like the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: They moved with the seasons following grass and water, much like the Turks.

sentences.zh: 有阿會氏，五部中爲盛，諸部皆歸之。

translations.literal: There was the Aihui clan, the most powerful among the five divisions, and all the divisions submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Aihui clan was the strongest of the five divisions, and all the others submitted to it.

sentences.zh: 每與契丹相攻擊，虜獲財畜，因而得賞。

translations.literal: They frequently attacked the Khitan, capturing goods and livestock and thus earning rewards.
translations.idiomatic: They regularly raided the Khitan, seizing goods and livestock and thereby earning rewards.

sentences.zh: 死者以葦薄裹屍，懸之樹上。

translations.literal: When a person died, the corpse was wrapped in reeds and hung on a tree.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were wrapped in reed mats and hung from trees.

sentences.zh: 自突厥稱籓之後，亦遣使入朝，或通或絕，最爲無信。

translations.literal: After the Turks submitted as vassals, the Xi also sent envoys to court, but contact was sometimes maintained and sometimes broken — they were the most untrustworthy of all.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turks submitted as vassals, the Xi too sent envoys to court, but relations were intermittent — of all the tribes, they were the least trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 大業時，歲遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye era they sent envoys yearly to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era they sent envoys each year bearing local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 契丹之先，與庫莫奚異種而同類，並爲慕容氏所破，俱竄於松、漠之間。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Khitan and the Kumo Xi were different tribes but of the same category; both were shattered by the Murong and fled together into the pines and deserts.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and the Kumo Xi were distinct tribes of the same broad family; both were broken by the Murong and fled together into the pine forests and desert wastes.

sentences.zh: 其後稍大，居黃龍之北數百里。

translations.literal: They gradually grew larger afterward and dwelt several hundred li north of Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: They gradually grew in strength and settled several hundred li north of Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 其俗頗與靺鞨同。

translations.literal: Their customs were largely the same as the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs closely resembled those of the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 好爲寇盜。

translations.literal: They were fond of raiding and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: They were given to raiding and robbery.

sentences.zh: 父母死而悲哭者，以爲不壯。

translations.literal: Those who wept and wailed when their parents died were regarded as weak.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who wept when parents died was considered weak.

sentences.zh: 但以其屍置於山樹之上，經三年之後，乃收其骨而焚之。

translations.literal: They simply placed the corpse on a mountain tree; after three years they gathered the bones and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: They simply placed the body in the trees on the mountains; after three years they collected the bones and burned them.

sentences.zh: 因酹而祝曰：「冬月時，向陽食。

translations.literal: Then they poured a libation and prayed, saying: "In the winter months, feed facing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: They poured a libation and prayed: "In the winter months, feed facing the sun.

sentences.zh: 若我射獵時，使我多得豬鹿。」

translations.literal: When I hunt, grant that I obtain many pigs and deer."
translations.idiomatic: When I hunt, grant me many pigs and deer."

sentences.zh: 其無禮頑嚚，于諸夷最甚。

translations.literal: Their lack of propriety and obstinate wickedness was the worst among all the barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In their lack of propriety and obstinate wickedness they surpassed every other barbarian people.

sentences.zh: 當後魏時，爲高麗所侵，部落萬餘口求內附，止于白貔河。

translations.literal: During Northern Wei they were invaded by Goguryeo; more than ten thousand mouths of the tribe sought to submit inward and halted at the Baipi River.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Wei, Goguryeo invaded them; more than ten thousand people of the tribe sought to submit to the court and halted at the Baipi River.

sentences.zh: 其後爲突厥所逼，又以萬家寄於高麗。

translations.literal: Later they were pressed by the Turks and again entrusted ten thousand households to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Later, pressed by the Turks, they again placed ten thousand households under Goguryeo's protection.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，率諸莫賀弗來謁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, leading all the mohefu, they came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, their mohefu chiefs led a delegation to pay homage at court.

sentences.zh: 五年，悉其衆款塞，高祖納之，聽居其故地。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they led their entire people to submit at the frontier passes; Emperor Gaozu accepted them and permitted them to dwell in their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the entire people came to the frontier to submit; Emperor Gaozu received them and allowed them to remain in their former territory.

sentences.zh: 六年，其諸部相攻擊，久不止，又與突厥相侵，高祖使使責讓之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year their divisions attacked one another without cease, and they also encroached on the Turks; Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year their divisions fought one another without end and also raided the Turks; Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to rebuke them.

sentences.zh: 其國遣使詣闕，頓顙謝罪。

translations.literal: Their state sent envoys to the capital, prostrating themselves and confessing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Their leaders sent envoys to the capital, knocking their foreheads to the ground in apology.

sentences.zh: 其後契丹別部出伏等背高麗，率衆內附。

translations.literal: Later Chufu and others of a separate Khitan division turned against Goguryeo and led their people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Chufu and others of a separate Khitan division broke with Goguryeo and led their followers to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 高祖納之，安置于渴奚那頡之北。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu accepted them and settled them north of Kexina Ir.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu received them and settled them north of Kexina Ir.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，其別部四千餘家背突厥來降。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, more than four thousand households of a separate division turned against the Turks and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era, more than four thousand households of a separate division broke with the Turks and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上方與突厥和好，重失遠人之心，悉令給糧還本，敕突厥撫納之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then on friendly terms with the Turks and feared losing the hearts of distant peoples; all were given grain and sent back to their homeland, and orders were issued for the Turks to soothe and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then reconciling with the Turks and feared alienating distant peoples; he supplied them all with grain and ordered them sent home, instructing the Turks to receive and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 固辭不去。

translations.literal: They firmly refused to leave.
translations.idiomatic: They steadfastly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 部落漸衆，遂北徙逐水草，當遼西正北二百里，依託紇臣水而居。

translations.literal: The tribe gradually grew numerous and moved northward following grass and water, two hundred li due north of Liaoxi, settling along the Gechen River.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe gradually grew in numbers, moved north following grass and water, and settled two hundred li due north of Liaoxi along the Gechen River.

sentences.zh: 東西亙五百里，南北三百里，分爲十部。

translations.literal: They extended five hundred li east to west and three hundred li north to south, divided into ten divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory stretched five hundred li east to west and three hundred li north to south, divided into ten divisions.

sentences.zh: 兵多者三千，少者千餘，逐寒暑，隨水草畜牧。

translations.literal: The largest had three thousand warriors, the smallest more than a thousand; they moved with the seasons and herded according to grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: The strongest divisions fielded three thousand warriors, the weakest more than a thousand; they moved with the seasons and herded wherever grass and water were found.

sentences.zh: 有征伐，則酋帥相與議之，興兵動衆合符契。

translations.literal: When there was a campaign, the division chiefs deliberated together; to raise troops and mobilize the masses they joined tally-tokens.
translations.idiomatic: When war was at hand, the chiefs deliberated together; to raise troops and mobilize the people they joined tally-tokens.

sentences.zh: 突厥沙缽略可汗遣吐屯潘垤統之。

translations.literal: Ishbara Qaghan of the Turks dispatched the tutun Pantie to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara Qaghan of the Turks sent the tutun Pantie to command them.

sentences.zh: 室韋，契丹之類也。

translations.literal: The Shiwei were of the same category as the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei belonged to the same broad family as the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 其南者爲契丹，在北者號室韋，分爲五部，不相總一，所謂南室韋、北室韋、缽室韋、深末怛室韋、大室韋。

translations.literal: Those to the south were the Khitan; those to the north were called the Shiwei, divided into five sections not united under one ruler — the Southern Shiwei, Northern Shiwei, Bo Shiwei, Shenmoda Shiwei, and Great Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Those to the south were the Khitan; those to the north were called the Shiwei, split into five sections under no single ruler — the Southern Shiwei, Northern Shiwei, Bo Shiwei, Shenmoda Shiwei, and Great Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 並無君長，人民貧弱，突厥常以三吐屯總領之。

translations.literal: None had chieftains; the people were poor and weak, and the Turks regularly placed three tutuns in overall command of them.
translations.idiomatic: None had chieftains of their own; the people were poor and weak, and the Turks regularly placed three tutuns over them.

sentences.zh: 南室韋在契丹北三千里，土地卑濕，至夏則移向西北貸勃、欠對二山，多草木，饒禽獸，又多蚊蚋，人皆巢居，以避其患。

translations.literal: The Southern Shiwei lay three thousand li north of the Khitan; the land was low and damp. In summer they moved northwest toward the two mountains of Daibo and Qiandui, where vegetation was abundant and game plentiful, but mosquitoes and gnats were also numerous; all lived in tree nests to escape the pest.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Shiwei lived three thousand li north of the Khitan on low, damp ground. In summer they moved northwest toward Mount Daibo and Mount Qiandui, where grass and game were plentiful but mosquitoes and gnats swarmed; everyone lived in tree nests to escape the pests.

sentences.zh: 漸分爲二十五部，每部有餘莫弗瞞咄，猶酋長也。

translations.literal: They gradually divided into twenty-five divisions; each division had a yemo fumoduo, equivalent to a chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: They gradually split into twenty-five divisions, each headed by a yemo fumoduo who served as chieftain.

sentences.zh: 死則子弟代立，嗣絕則擇賢豪而立之。

translations.literal: When one died a son succeeded; if the line ended, a worthy and powerful man was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When a chieftain died, a son succeeded him; if the line died out, a worthy and powerful man was chosen.

sentences.zh: 其俗丈夫皆被發，婦人盤發，衣服與契丹同。

translations.literal: By custom the men wore their hair loose; the women wore their hair coiled; their clothing was the same as the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The men wore their hair loose and the women wore theirs coiled; their dress was the same as the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 乘牛車，籧篨爲屋，如突厥氈車之狀。

translations.literal: They rode ox-carts and made dwellings of bamboo matting, shaped like the Turks' felt carts.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled in ox-carts and made dwellings of woven matting, shaped like the Turks' felt-walled carts.

sentences.zh: 渡水則束薪爲栰，或以皮爲舟者。

translations.literal: To cross water they bound firewood into rafts, or sometimes made boats of hide.
translations.idiomatic: To cross rivers they bound firewood into rafts, or sometimes made boats of hide.

sentences.zh: 馬則織草爲韉，結繩爲轡。

translations.literal: For horses they wove grass into saddles and knotted rope into bridles.
translations.idiomatic: For horses they wove grass into saddles and knotted rope into bridles.

sentences.zh: 寢則屈爲屋，以籧篨覆上，移則載行。

translations.literal: When sleeping they bent materials into a dwelling and covered it with bamboo matting, loading it for transport when they moved.
translations.idiomatic: For shelter they bent poles into a frame, covered it with matting, and loaded the whole structure onto carts when they moved.

sentences.zh: 以豬皮爲席，編木爲藉。

translations.literal: They used pig hide for mats and wove wood for bedding.
translations.idiomatic: They used pig hide for mats and wove wood into bedding platforms.

sentences.zh: 婦女皆抱膝而坐。

translations.literal: All women sat hugging their knees.
translations.idiomatic: Women always sat with their knees drawn up.

sentences.zh: 氣候多寒，田收甚薄，無羊，少馬，多豬牛。

translations.literal: The climate was mostly cold, harvests very meager; they had no sheep, few horses, but many pigs and cattle.
