translations.idiomatic: The climate was bitterly cold, harvests meager; they kept no sheep, few horses, but many pigs and cattle.

sentences.zh: 造酒食啖，與靺鞨同俗。

translations.literal: They made fermented drinks and consumed them — a custom the same as the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: They brewed fermented drink and consumed it — a custom shared with the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁之法，二家相許，婿輒盜婦將去，然後送牛馬爲娉，更將歸家。

translations.literal: The method of marriage: when two families had agreed, the bridegroom would steal the bride away, then send cattle and horses as betrothal gifts and take her back to her home.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage, once two families had agreed, the bridegroom would steal the bride away, then send cattle and horses as betrothal gifts and return her to her family.

sentences.zh: 待有娠，乃相隨還舍。

translations.literal: When she became pregnant, only then did husband and wife return together to their dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Only once she was pregnant did husband and wife return together to their home.

sentences.zh: 婦人不再嫁，以爲死人之妻難以共居。

translations.literal: Women did not remarry, on the ground that a dead man's wife was hard to live with.
translations.idiomatic: Women did not remarry, believing that a dead man's wife was unfit to live with another.

sentences.zh: 部落共爲大棚，人死則置屍其上。

translations.literal: The tribe jointly built a great shed; when a person died the corpse was placed atop it.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe built a communal great shed; when someone died, the body was placed on top of it.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，年唯四哭。

translations.literal: Mourning lasted three years, with wailing only on four days of the year.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning lasted three years, but they wailed on only four days each year.

sentences.zh: 其國無鐵，取給於高麗。

translations.literal: Their country had no iron; they obtained it from Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: They had no iron of their own and obtained it from Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 多貂。

translations.literal: Sables were plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Sables were abundant.

sentences.zh: 南室韋北行十一日至北室韋，分爲九部落，繞吐紇山而居。

translations.literal: Eleven days' travel north from the Southern Shiwei brought one to the Northern Shiwei, divided into nine tribal sections dwelling around Mount Tuohe.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven days' travel north from the Southern Shiwei brought one to the Northern Shiwei, divided into nine tribal sections living around Mount Tuohe.

sentences.zh: 其部落渠帥號乞引莫賀咄，每部有莫何弗三人以貳之。

translations.literal: The division chieftains were called qiyin moheduo; each division had three mohefu as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Division chiefs were styled qiyin moheduo; each division had three mohefu as deputies.

sentences.zh: 氣候最寒，雪深沒馬。

translations.literal: The climate was the coldest of all; snow lay deep enough to bury horses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was the bitterest of all; snow lay deep enough to bury horses.

sentences.zh: 冬則入山，居土穴中，牛畜多凍死。

translations.literal: In winter they entered the mountains and lived in earthen pits; many cattle and livestock froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they retreated into the mountains and lived in earthen pits; many cattle and livestock froze to death.

sentences.zh: 饒麞鹿，射獵爲務，食肉衣皮。

translations.literal: Sable-deer were plentiful; hunting was their chief occupation; they ate meat and wore skins.
translations.idiomatic: Sable-deer were plentiful; hunting was their chief occupation; they ate meat and wore skins.

sentences.zh: 鑿冰，沒水中而網射魚鱉。

translations.literal: They cut through ice and submerged nets in the water to shoot fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: They cut through ice, lowered nets into the water, and shot fish and turtles.

sentences.zh: 地多積雪，懼陷坑阱，騎木而行。

translations.literal: Snow accumulated deeply on the ground; fearing pits and traps, they traveled by riding wooden boards.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay deep on the ground; fearing hidden pits, they traveled by riding wooden boards.

sentences.zh: 俗皆捕貂爲業，冠以狐狢，衣以魚皮。

translations.literal: By custom all hunted sable for a livelihood; they wore caps of fox and raccoon dog and clothes of fish skin.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they all hunted sable for a living; they wore caps of fox and raccoon dog fur and clothes of fish skin.

sentences.zh: 又北行千里，至缽室韋，依胡布山而住，人衆多北室韋，不知爲幾部落。

translations.literal: Another thousand li northward brought one to the Bo Shiwei, dwelling along Mount Hubu; their population exceeded that of the Northern Shiwei, but how many tribal sections they comprised is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Another thousand li north brought one to the Bo Shiwei, who lived along Mount Hubu; their numbers exceeded those of the Northern Shiwei, though how many tribal sections they comprised is unknown.

sentences.zh: 用樺皮蓋屋，其餘同北室韋。

translations.literal: They roofed houses with birch bark; in other respects they were the same as the Northern Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: They roofed their dwellings with birch bark; in all other respects they resembled the Northern Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 從缽室韋西南四日行，至深末怛室韋，因水爲號也。

translations.literal: Four days' travel southwest from the Bo Shiwei brought one to the Shenmoda Shiwei — they took their name from the river.
translations.idiomatic: Four days' travel southwest from the Bo Shiwei brought one to the Shenmoda Shiwei, who took their name from the river.

sentences.zh: 冬月穴居，以避太陰之氣。

translations.literal: In winter months they dwelt in pits to escape the yin cold.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they lived in pit dwellings to escape the penetrating cold.

sentences.zh: 又西北數千里，至大室韋，徑路險阻，語言不通。

translations.literal: Another several thousand li northwestward brought one to the Great Shiwei; the routes were perilous, and speech was mutually unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand li farther northwest lay the Great Shiwei; the routes were perilous and their speech was unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 尤多貂及青鼠。

translations.literal: Sables and blue rats were especially plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Sables and blue rats were especially abundant.

sentences.zh: 北室韋時遣使貢獻，餘無至者。

translations.literal: The Northern Shiwei occasionally sent envoys with tribute; the others never came.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Northern Shiwei occasionally sent envoys bearing tribute; the others never came.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四夷之爲中國患也久矣，北狄尤甚焉。

translations.literal: The historians say: The Four Barbarians have long been a calamity to China, and the Northern Di have been especially so.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: The Four Barbarians have long been a scourge to China, and the Northern Di above all.

sentences.zh: 種落實繁，迭雄邊塞，年代遐邈，非一時也。

translations.literal: Their tribes and clans are truly numerous; they have successively dominated the frontier in ages remote and distant — not in one period alone.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes and clans are truly numerous; they have risen in turn to dominate the frontier across ages remote and distant — not in one era alone.

sentences.zh: 五帝之世，則有獯粥焉；

translations.literal: In the age of the Five Emperors there was Xunyu;
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Five Emperors there was Xunyu;

sentences.zh: 其在三代，則獫狁焉；

translations.literal: in the Three Dynasties there was Xianyun;
translations.idiomatic: in the Three Dynasties there was Xianyun;

sentences.zh: 逮乎兩漢，則匈奴焉；

translations.literal: by the two Han dynasties there was the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: by the two Han dynasties there was the Xiongnu;

sentences.zh: 當塗、典午，則烏丸、鮮卑焉；

translations.literal: under the Han and Jin there were the Wuhuan and Xianbei;
translations.idiomatic: under the Han and Jin there were the Wuhuan and Xianbei;

sentences.zh: 後魏及周，則蠕蠕、突厥焉。

translations.literal: in Later Wei and Zhou there were the Rouran and Turks.
translations.idiomatic: in Northern Wei and Northern Zhou there were the Rouran and Turks.

sentences.zh: 此其酋豪，相繼互爲君長者也。

translations.literal: These were their chieftains and heroes, who succeeded one another as rulers.
translations.idiomatic: These were their chieftains and strongmen, succeeding one another as rulers.

sentences.zh: 皆以畜牧爲業，侵鈔爲資，倏來忽往，雲飛鳥集。

translations.literal: All took herding as their occupation and raiding as their sustenance — coming and going in an instant, gathering and dispersing like clouds and birds in flight.
translations.idiomatic: All lived by herding and sustained themselves by raiding — appearing and vanishing in an instant, gathering and scattering like clouds and birds on the wing.

sentences.zh: 智謀之士，議和親於廟堂之上，折沖之臣，論奮擊於塞垣之下。

translations.literal: Men of counsel debated marital alliances in the hall of government; ministers charged with repelling the enemy discussed striking blows at the frontier fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors debated marriage alliances in the imperial hall; frontier generals argued for bold strikes below the border walls.

sentences.zh: 然事無恆規，權無定勢，親疏因其強弱，服叛在其盛衰。

translations.literal: Yet affairs had no fixed rule, and power no settled balance; closeness or distance followed strength or weakness, submission or rebellion followed rise or decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet policy had no fixed rule and power no settled balance — intimacy or distance followed strength and weakness; submission or rebellion followed rise and decline.

sentences.zh: 衰則款塞頓顙，盛則彎弓寇掠，屈申異態，強弱相反。

translations.literal: When weak they submitted at the passes and knocked their foreheads to the ground; when strong they bent their bows and raided — their postures of yielding and extending differed, strength and weakness reversed.
translations.idiomatic: When weak they came to the frontier passes and knocked their foreheads to the ground; when strong they bent their bows and raided — their postures of submission and aggression reversed with the shift of power.

sentences.zh: 正朔所不及，冠帶所不加，唯利是視，不顧盟誓。

translations.literal: Beyond the reach of the imperial calendar and ungirdled by cap and sash, they looked only to profit and paid no heed to oaths and treaties.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the reach of the imperial calendar and the constraints of civilization, they looked only to profit and cared nothing for oaths and treaties.

sentences.zh: 至於莫相救讓，驕黠憑陵，和親約結之謀，行師用兵之事，前史論之備矣，故不詳而究焉。

translations.literal: As for their failure to aid and defer to one another, their arrogance and cunning in imposing on others, and the schemes of marriage alliances and the business of marching armies — earlier histories have discussed these fully, so they are not treated in detail here.
translations.idiomatic: As for their refusal to aid or yield to one another, their arrogance and cunning in imposing on others, and the whole history of marriage alliances and military campaigns — earlier histories have treated these at length, and they are not rehearsed in detail here.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕衰微，突厥始大，至於木杆，遂雄朔野。

translations.literal: When the Rouran declined and the Turks first grew great, down to Mughan, they dominated the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran declined and the Turks first rose to power, Mughan came to dominate the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 東極東胡舊境，西盡烏孫之地，彎弓數十萬，列處於代陰，南向以臨周、齊。

translations.literal: Eastward they reached the old lands of the Eastern Hu, westward they extended to the territory of the Wusun; with bows bent, several hundred thousand strong, they were arrayed north of Dai, facing south to menace Zhou and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward their domain reached the old lands of the Eastern Hu; westward it extended to Wusun territory. With several hundred thousand warriors under arms, they camped north of Dai, facing south to threaten Northern Zhou and Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 二國莫之能抗，爭請盟好，求結和親。

translations.literal: Neither state could resist them; both vied to request alliance and sought marriage ties.
translations.idiomatic: Neither state could resist them. Both vied to request alliance and sought marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 乃與周合從，終亡齊國。

translations.literal: They then joined with Zhou in alliance and ultimately destroyed the Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: They then allied with Northern Zhou and ultimately destroyed Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷鼎，厥徒孔熾，負其衆力，將蹈秦郊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu moved the capital, their followers were exceedingly fierce; relying on their multitude of strength, they were about to tread the Qin suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, their followers were exceedingly fierce. Relying on their numbers, they were poised to raid the Qin heartland.

sentences.zh: 內自相圖，遂以乖亂，達頭可汗遠遁，啟民願保塞下。

translations.literal: Internally they plotted against one another and thus fell into discord; Tardu Qaghan fled far away, and Qimin wished to hold the area below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted against one another and fell into discord. Tardu Qaghan fled far away, while Qimin sought protection south of the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 於是推亡固存，返其舊地，助討餘燼，部衆遂強。

translations.literal: Thereupon, supporting the perishing and strengthening the surviving, their old lands were restored; aided in suppressing the remaining embers, their followers grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui court supported the perishing and strengthened the surviving, restored their old lands, and aided in suppressing the remaining embers. Their followers grew strong.

sentences.zh: 卒于仁壽，不侵不叛，暨乎始畢，未虧臣禮。

translations.literal: Until the end of the Renshou era they neither invaded nor rebelled; down to Shibi, they did not fall short in the duties of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Until the end of the Renshou era they neither invaded nor rebelled. Down to Shibi's reign, they did not fall short in the duties of subjects.

sentences.zh: 煬帝撫之非道，始有雁門之圍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang treated them improperly, and thus arose the siege at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang treated them improperly, and thus arose the siege at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 俄屬群盜並興，於此浸以雄盛，豪傑雖建名號，莫不請好息民。

translations.literal: Soon, as bandits rose everywhere, they gradually grew mighty from this; though heroes established titles, none failed to request peace and rest for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as rebellion spread everywhere, they gradually grew mighty. Though rival warlords established their own titles, none failed to sue for peace and seek their favor.

sentences.zh: 於是分置官司，總統中國，子女玉帛，相繼于道，使者之車，往來結轍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established offices and governed the Central States; sons and daughters, jade and silks, followed one upon another on the roads; envoys' carriages came and went with wheels overlapping.
translations.idiomatic: They established offices and held sway over the Central States. Tribute of sons and daughters, jade and silks, flowed endlessly along the roads, and envoys' carriages came and went with wheels overlapping.

sentences.zh: 自古蕃夷驕僭，未有若斯之甚也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, no barbarian arrogance and usurpation has ever reached such an extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, no barbarian arrogance and usurpation has ever reached such an extreme.

sentences.zh: 及聖哲膺期，掃除氛昆，暗于時變，猶懷旅拒，率其群醜，屢隳亭鄣，殘毀我雲、代，搖盪我太原，肆掠于涇陽，飲馬於渭汭。

translations.literal: When the sage and wise received the mandate, sweeping away miasma and turmoil, blind to the changing times, they still harbored resistance as strangers; leading their wicked hordes, they repeatedly destroyed beacon towers and fortifications, ravaged our Yun and Dai, shook our Taiyuan, plundered freely at Jingyang, and watered their horses at the Wei River bend.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage emperor received the mandate and swept away chaos, the Turks—blind to the changing times—still harbored defiance. Leading their wicked hordes, they repeatedly destroyed frontier fortifications, ravaged Yun and Dai, shook Taiyuan, plundered Jingyang, and watered their horses at the Wei River bend.

sentences.zh: 聖上奇謀潛運，神機密動，遂使百世不羈之虜一舉而滅，瀚海龍庭之地，畫爲九州，幽都窮發之民，隸於編戶，實帝皇所不及，書契所未聞。

translations.literal: The sage emperor's wondrous stratagems worked in secret, divine schemes moved covertly; thus the barbarians unrestrained for a hundred generations were destroyed in a single stroke. The lands of the vast sea and dragon court were marked as the Nine Provinces; the people of the remote north and uttermost regions were enrolled in household registers—truly what emperors and sovereigns had not achieved, what written records had never recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor's wondrous stratagems worked in secret, his divine schemes moved covertly, and the barbarians unrestrained for a hundred generations were destroyed in a single stroke. The lands of the northern sea and dragon court were marked as the Nine Provinces; the people of the remote north were enrolled in household registers—an achievement no emperor had matched, an event no written record had ever recorded.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，雖天道有盛衰，亦人事之工拙也。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, though Heaven's Way has rise and decline, it is also a matter of human effort—skillful or clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that though Heaven's Way has its cycles of rise and decline, human effort—skillful or clumsy—also plays its part.

sentences.zh: 加以爲而弗恃，有而弗居，類天地之含容，同陰陽之化育，斯乃大道之行也，固無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, acting yet not relying on it, possessing yet not dwelling in it—resembling Heaven and Earth's all-embracing tolerance, matching yin and yang's nurturing transformation—this is the Way's fulfillment, and truly there is no adequate way to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, acting yet not boasting of it, possessing yet not dwelling in it—resembling Heaven and Earth's all-embracing tolerance, matching yin and yang's nurturing transformation—this is the fulfillment of the Great Way, and truly there are no words adequate to praise it.
